title: Asthma exacerbation
summary: Admit to CTU/ward if improving and supportable on the asthma pathway; step-down/PICU for continuous salbutamol, escalating oxygen, exhaustion, altered mental status, silent chest, hypercapnia, or poor response after intensive initial therapy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward if improving and supportable on the asthma pathway; step-down/PICU for continuous salbutamol, escalating oxygen, exhaustion, altered mental status, silent chest, hypercapnia, or poor response after intensive initial therapy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h during frequent bronchodilators, then q4h once clearly improving; record PRAM or the hospital respiratory score before and after treatments.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry while hypoxemic or receiving q1h/continuous therapy; cardiorespiratory monitoring during continuous salbutamol or IV magnesium; strict intake/output if IV fluids.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen to the hospital target. Salbutamol by MDI/spacer: <20 kg 5 puffs (500 mcg), >=20 kg 10 puffs (1000 mcg), or nebulized 2.5 mg/5 mg respectively; repeat/space by pathway. Add ipratropium for the first 3 severe treatments.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for severe disease, dehydration, IV magnesium, continuous therapy, or uncertain trajectory; consider a second line if critically ill.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Oral fluids if safe; NPO during severe distress. Use cautious isotonic IV maintenance/deficit replacement; avoid routine fluid boluses unless perfusion is poor.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: None routinely. Obtain VBG/CBG, glucose, potassium and lactate only for severe disease, fatigue, prolonged continuous beta-agonist, or diagnostic uncertainty.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine chest radiograph. Obtain for focal/asymmetric findings, pneumothorax, foreign body, significant fever/complication, or unexpected poor response.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give systemic steroid early: dexamethasone 0.3-0.6 mg/kg PO/IV once (max 10-16 mg per local order set) or prednisone/prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day (max 50 mg). For severe refractory disease give magnesium sulfate 40-75 mg/kg IV over 20-30 min (max 2.5 g).

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: RT and senior early for moderate-severe disease; PICU for continuous therapy, rising support, hypercapnia, exhaustion, altered mentation, or poor air entry; anesthesia if impending airway/ventilatory failure.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Document score, oxygen, air entry and response before/after each treatment; record salbutamol interval; teach spacer technique when stable; avoid sedatives.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess after every initial treatment and at least q1-2h until stable. If not improving after 3 intensive treatments/steroid, treat as severe, give magnesium, call PICU and prepare escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen to the hospital target. Salbutamol by MDI/spacer: <20 kg 5 puffs (500 mcg), >=20 kg 10 puffs (1000 mcg), or nebulized 2.5 mg/5 mg respectively; repeat/space by pathway. Add ipratropium for the first 3 severe treatments.

Medications/treatments: Give systemic steroid early: dexamethasone 0.3-0.6 mg/kg PO/IV once (max 10-16 mg per local order set) or prednisone/prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day (max 50 mg). For severe refractory disease give magnesium sulfate 40-75 mg/kg IV over 20-30 min (max 2.5 g).

title: Bronchiolitis
summary: Admit to Ward for supportive care; step-down/PICU for apnea, escalating oxygen/flow, exhaustion, hypercapnia, or hemodynamic instability.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for supportive care; step-down/PICU for apnea, escalating oxygen/flow, exhaustion, hypercapnia, or hemodynamic instability.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h based on severity; q1-2h during escalation. Continuous monitoring for apnea, oxygen/HFNC or very young/high-risk infant; reduce monitoring once stable to avoid reacting to transient desaturation.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals and respiratory assessments; pulse oximetry while oxygen-dependent or high risk; avoid unnecessary continuous monitoring once stable per hospital pathway.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Low-flow oxygen then local high-flow pathway if indicated; nasal saline and superficial suction before feeds; no routine chest physiotherapy.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Not mandatory if drinking; obtain for IV fluids or significant illness.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral/NG preferred where safe; isotonic IV fluids if needed, with glucose/electrolytes as age dictates.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: No routine labs; consider glucose, gas, electrolytes, cultures only for severe illness, apnea, dehydration, very young infant or alternate diagnosis.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine CXR; reserve for severe/atypical course, focal findings, ICU planning, or concern for complication.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Supportive care. Do not routinely use salbutamol, corticosteroids, antibiotics, nebulized epinephrine, hypertonic saline or chest physiotherapy. Treat a clearly identified alternate diagnosis only.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: RT for escalating support; PICU for apnea/failure; consider pediatrics/feeding support in high-risk infant.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Suction before feeds and PRN; record percentage feeds and wet diapers; document apnea events and response to oxygen.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess after suction/oxygen changes and at least every 2â€“4 hours depending on severity; anticipate peak illness around days 3â€“5.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Low-flow oxygen then local high-flow pathway if indicated; nasal saline and superficial suction before feeds; no routine chest physiotherapy.

Medications/treatments: Supportive care. Do not routinely use salbutamol, corticosteroids, antibiotics, nebulized epinephrine, hypertonic saline or chest physiotherapy. Treat a clearly identified alternate diagnosis only.

title: Preschool viral-induced wheeze
summary: Admit to CTU/ward if the child requires bronchodilator more frequently than the local discharge threshold, needs oxygen/IV hydration, or has an uncertain trajectory; step-down/PICU for continuous therapy, exhaustion, recurrent apnea, or escalating support.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward if the child requires bronchodilator more frequently than the local discharge threshold, needs oxygen/IV hydration, or has an uncertain trajectory; step-down/PICU for continuous therapy, exhaustion, recurrent apnea, or escalating support.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h while improving; q1-2h during frequent treatments or if severity is changing. Record a consistent respiratory score with each treatment.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry while hypoxemic or receiving frequent therapy; cardiorespiratory monitoring for severe disease or continuous beta-agonist.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Titrate oxygen to the local target. Give inhaled short-acting beta-agonist by MDI/spacer or nebulizer per pathway; call RT if response is incomplete or technique is uncertain.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Not routinely needed if drinking and improving; obtain if severe, dehydrated, requiring IV therapy, or diagnosis is uncertain.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Encourage oral fluids; use isotonic IV fluids if intake is inadequate. Avoid unnecessary fluid loading.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: None routinely. Consider blood gas, electrolytes, glucose, and potassium only for severe disease, fatigue, prolonged beta-agonist exposure, or another diagnosis.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine chest radiograph. Obtain only for focal findings, asymmetric air entry, fever with suspected complication, foreign-body concern, pneumothorax, or poor response.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Bronchodilator per pathway; systemic corticosteroid for moderate/severe or recurrent steroid-responsive episodes; do not routinely prescribe antibiotics. Verify dose and age eligibility locally.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior/RT for moderate-severe disease; PICU for continuous therapy or deterioration; respiratory/asthma team if recurrent admissions or diagnostic uncertainty.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT: Document pre/post-treatment score, bronchodilator interval, oxygen need, intake, spacer technique, and sleep response; avoid sedating medications.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after each initial treatment and at least q1-2h until clearly improving; escalate for silent chest, reduced effort with poor air entry, rising CO2, altered mental status, or increasing oxygen/support.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Titrate oxygen to the local target. Give inhaled short-acting beta-agonist by MDI/spacer or nebulizer per pathway; call RT if response is incomplete or technique is uncertain.

Medications/treatments: Bronchodilator per pathway; systemic corticosteroid for moderate/severe or recurrent steroid-responsive episodes; do not routinely prescribe antibiotics. Verify dose and age eligibility locally.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Community-acquired pneumonia
summary: Admit to Ward if stable; step-down/PICU for respiratory failure, shock, large/complicated effusion, necrotizing disease, or need for noninvasive/invasive ventilation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward if stable; step-down/PICU for respiratory failure, shock, large/complicated effusion, necrotizing disease, or need for noninvasive/invasive ventilation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals, respiratory assessments, pulse oximetry while hypoxemic; strict I&O in significant illness; cardiac monitoring if unstable.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen to local target; HFNC/NIV only with appropriate monitoring and escalation plan.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if admitted for parenteral antibiotics, dehydration, toxicity or possible complication.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral as tolerated; isotonic IV fluids if needed; bolus only for shock and reassess frequently.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, blood culture and inflammatory markers for severe/complicated disease; electrolytes if IV fluids; viral testing when it changes isolation/treatment; targeted tests by context.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: CXR for admitted moderate-severe disease, hypoxemia, failed therapy or complication; ultrasound for effusion; avoid routine repeat imaging if improving.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: For uncomplicated bacterial CAP in an immunized child, use ampicillin IV or amoxicillin PO when local pneumococcal susceptibility permits; ceftriaxone for severe disease, incomplete immunization or local indication. Add azithromycin only when atypical pneumonia is plausible; add vancomycin/clindamycin for MRSA/necrotizing features. Verify local antibiogram and allergy history.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior for all complicated cases; ID/respirology for severe or unusual infection; surgery/IR for drainable effusion; PICU for organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Track oxygen, fever curve, pain, intake and antibiotic timing; obtain cultures before antibiotics only if this does not delay treatment.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess within 1â€“2 hours after admission/support changes and at least every 4 hours; lack of improvement by 24â€“48 hours prompts complication review.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen to local target; HFNC/NIV only with appropriate monitoring and escalation plan.

Medications/treatments: For uncomplicated bacterial CAP in an immunized child, use ampicillin IV or amoxicillin PO when local pneumococcal susceptibility permits; ceftriaxone for severe disease, incomplete immunization or local indication. Add azithromycin only when atypical pneumonia is plausible; add vancomycin/clindamycin for MRSA/necrotizing features. Verify local antibiogram and allergy history.

title: Complicated pneumonia / empyema
summary: Admit to CTU/ward with early senior review; step-down/PICU for shock, substantial respiratory support, altered mental status, severe work of breathing, or rapidly progressive disease.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward with early senior review; step-down/PICU for shock, substantial respiratory support, altered mental status, severe work of breathing, or rapidly progressive disease.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if stable; more frequently during respiratory compromise, fever-associated instability, or after procedures.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry while hypoxemic; strict I&O; cardiorespiratory monitoring if unstable, receiving significant opioids, or after drainage.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen to local target; RT airway clearance only when indicated. Avoid routine aggressive chest physiotherapy over a painful effusion.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; consider a second line if septic, procedure likely, or fluid/antibiotic needs are substantial.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Encourage oral intake when safe; isotonic IV fluids if needed. Avoid fluid overload and reassess urine output/perfusion.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/differential, CRP or other local inflammatory marker, electrolytes/renal function, blood culture before antibiotics when feasible; pleural fluid studies/culture if drained.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph and lung ultrasound; CT only for selected complex anatomy, alternative diagnosis, or surgical planning after specialist discussion.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start empiric IV antibiotics covering typical pathogens and local resistance patterns; analgesia and antipyretics; drainage strategy per ultrasound, clinical course, and hospital pathway. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Infectious diseases and interventional radiology/respirology/surgery according to local drainage model; PICU early if support is escalating.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT: Measure oxygen requirement, pain, fever curve, fluid balance, chest-drain output/air leak, and work of breathing; maintain drain system and specimen handling per policy.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess within 1-2h after stabilization and at least q4h; urgent escalation for worsening oxygen need, shock, increasing effusion, persistent severe distress, drain malfunction, or clinical deterioration despite antibiotics.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen to local target; RT airway clearance only when indicated. Avoid routine aggressive chest physiotherapy over a painful effusion.

Medications/treatments: Start empiric IV antibiotics covering typical pathogens and local resistance patterns; analgesia and antipyretics; drainage strategy per ultrasound, clinical course, and hospital pathway. Verify doses.

title: Croup
summary: Admit to ward for persistent stridor at rest, repeated nebulized epinephrine, oxygen need, poor intake, high-risk airway, or unreliable observation; PICU/anesthesia for fatigue, cyanosis, reduced air entry, altered mental status, or impending obstruction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to ward for persistent stridor at rest, repeated nebulized epinephrine, oxygen need, poor intake, high-risk airway, or unreliable observation; PICU/anesthesia for fatigue, cyanosis, reduced air entry, altered mental status, or impending obstruction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2h initially after epinephrine, then q4h when stable; minimize agitation and unnecessary examinations.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry while stridor at rest, hypoxemic, asleep after severe symptoms, or within the observation period after epinephrine.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Keep child upright and calm; blow-by oxygen if needed. Avoid forcing a mask. Prepare difficult-airway equipment if severe.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Avoid distressing procedures in a stable child; obtain only if severe, dehydrated, toxic, or another diagnosis is suspected.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Oral fluids as tolerated once breathing is settled; NPO if severe obstruction or airway intervention may be required; isotonic IV fluids if unable to drink.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: None routinely. Blood gas only with severe fatigue/impending respiratory failure; test for alternate infection only when clinically indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely. Neck/chest imaging only if atypical presentation or concern for foreign body, bacterial tracheitis, retropharyngeal abscess, or epiglottitisâ€”and only if airway is stable.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg PO/IM/IV once (commonly max 10 mg; verify hospital maximum). For stridor at rest give nebulized racemic epinephrine 2.25% 0.5 mL diluted to ~3 mL, or L-epinephrine 1 mg/mL 5 mL, according to available product; reassess promptly and observe at least 2-3 h after the last dose.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior/RT for moderate-severe croup; anesthesia/ENT/PICU immediately for severe obstruction, recurrent epinephrine need, atypical course, drooling/tripod posture, toxic appearance, or suspected bacterial airway disease.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Cluster care, keep caregiver present, document stridor at rest versus agitation, retractions, air entry and time of each epinephrine dose; keep emergency airway equipment available for severe disease.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess 10-20 min after epinephrine and serially through the 2-3 h rebound window. Recurrent stridor at rest or worsening fatigue requires senior/PICU/airway escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Keep child upright and calm; blow-by oxygen if needed. Avoid forcing a mask. Prepare difficult-airway equipment if severe.

Medications/treatments: Dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg PO/IM/IV once (commonly max 10 mg; verify hospital maximum). For stridor at rest give nebulized racemic epinephrine 2.25% 0.5 mL diluted to ~3 mL, or L-epinephrine 1 mg/mL 5 mL, according to available product; reassess promptly and observe at least 2-3 h after the last dose.

title: Apnea in an infant
summary: Admit to monitored ward/step-down for documented apnea, recurrent cyanotic episodes or need for stimulation; PICU for bag-mask ventilation, recurrent significant apnea, hypercapnia, hemodynamic instability or uncertain airway.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored ward/step-down for documented apnea, recurrent cyanotic episodes or need for stimulation; PICU for bag-mask ventilation, recurrent significant apnea, hypercapnia, hemodynamic instability or uncertain airway.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous during events; q1-2h initially, then q4h only after a stable period.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory and pulse-ox monitoring; document event duration, tracing, relation to feed/sleep, stimulation and recovery.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Position/suction, oxygen and bag-mask ventilation as required; HFNC/CPAP or caffeine only for an identified indication with senior/PICU/neonatal guidance.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if recurrent, abnormal exam, planned testing or unable to feed safely.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Maintenance only if NPO; treat glucose abnormality.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Point-of-care glucose often reasonable; ECG; targeted CBC/cultures/viral testing, gas, electrolytes, toxicology or neurologic studies only by findingsâ€”not a shotgun panel.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine imaging; CXR, neuroimaging or skeletal survey only for specific indications.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat the causeâ€”antibiotics for sepsis, bronchiolitis support, seizure treatment, reflux/aspiration plan, or neonatal caffeine when specifically indicated. Do not label recurrent true apnea as BRUE.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior review; cardiology, neurology, feeding/ENT, child protection or PICU guided by features.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Ask staff to document every eventâ€™s duration, breathing effort, color, tone, monitor rhythm and intervention; supervised feed if ordered.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review every event immediately. Any event requiring vigorous stimulation/ventilation, increasing frequency, abnormal gas, poor feeding or altered exam requires PICU and cause-directed evaluation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Position/suction, oxygen and bag-mask ventilation as required; HFNC/CPAP or caffeine only for an identified indication with senior/PICU/neonatal guidance.

Medications/treatments: Treat the causeâ€”antibiotics for sepsis, bronchiolitis support, seizure treatment, reflux/aspiration plan, or neonatal caffeine when specifically indicated. Do not label recurrent true apnea as BRUE.

title: Higher-risk BRUE
summary: Admit only when the resolved event is higher risk because of recurrent events, concerning history/exam, significant prematurity/comorbidity, abnormal testing, safeguarding concern, poor feeding, or unreliable follow-up; a low-risk BRUE generally needs brief observation rather than admission.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit only when the resolved event is higher risk because of recurrent events, concerning history/exam, significant prematurity/comorbidity, abnormal testing, safeguarding concern, poor feeding, or unreliable follow-up; a low-risk BRUE generally needs brief observation rather than admission.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if admitted and well; more frequent during recurrence or if an alternate diagnosis emerges.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Cardiorespiratory and pulse-ox monitoring during observation/admission; document whether any event is objectively witnessed and its duration/features.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: None if baseline; oxygen/suction only for documented hypoxemia or an identified respiratory disorder. Recurrent apnea requiring stimulation or ventilation is not a simple BRUE and needs PICU assessment.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Not routine; obtain if recurrent events, poor feeding, infection/metabolic concern, or treatment is needed.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Continue observed feeds if safe; feeding assessment if choking/coughing, poor coordination or aspiration concern. IV/NG support only for an identified need.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: No blanket panel. Target glucose, CBC/cultures, electrolytes, ECG, pertussis/viral testing, toxicology or other tests to specific history/exam findings.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine CXR, neuroimaging, skeletal survey or reflux studies. Order only when a specific alternate diagnosis or maltreatment concern is present.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: No empiric acid suppression, caffeine or home monitor for an unexplained resolved event. Treat the identified cause; provide caregiver CPR education/resources.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior pediatrics; feeding/SLP, cardiology, neurology, respirology or child protection only when indicated by findings; PICU for recurrent significant apnea or instability.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Use event documentation sheetâ€”colour, tone, breathing, responsiveness, duration, monitor tracing, intervention and relation to feed/sleep; safe-sleep education.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review after approximately 4 h observation and after a feed. Any recurrent/prolonged event, abnormal vitals/exam, seizure-like activity, trauma or safeguarding concern triggers a diagnosis-directed evaluation and higher level of care.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None if baseline; oxygen/suction only for documented hypoxemia or an identified respiratory disorder. Recurrent apnea requiring stimulation or ventilation is not a simple BRUE and needs PICU assessment.
Medications/treatments: No empiric acid suppression, caffeine or home monitor for an unexplained resolved event. Treat the identified cause; provide caregiver CPR education/resources.

title: Aspiration event / aspiration pneumonia
summary: Admit to CTU/ward for persistent oxygen need, respiratory distress, recurrent aspiration, inability to protect the airway, significant comorbidity, or feeding-safety concern; PICU for escalating support or impaired airway protection.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward for persistent oxygen need, respiratory distress, recurrent aspiration, inability to protect the airway, significant comorbidity, or feeding-safety concern; PICU for escalating support or impaired airway protection.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h depending on respiratory status; increase frequency after a witnessed event or any deterioration.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry initially; cardiorespiratory monitoring for apnea, neurologic impairment, significant sedative exposure, or severe disease.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Position and suction as needed; titrate oxygen; involve RT for secretion clearance and escalation. Avoid routine deep suctioning when not indicated.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain if moderate/severe disease, poor intake, anticipated IV antibiotics, or uncertain trajectory.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO initially if airway protection or swallow safety is uncertain; isotonic IV fluids as needed. Resume feeds only after a clear safety plan.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Usually none after a brief uncomplicated event. Consider CBC, gas, electrolytes, cultures, and lactate for severe illness, sepsis, or prolonged hypoxemia.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph for persistent symptoms, focal findings, oxygen need, or suspected complication; early imaging can be normal.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Supportive care for chemical pneumonitis; start antibiotics only when bacterial aspiration pneumonia is suspected or symptoms persist/evolve, using local guidance. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: SLP/feeding team for swallow assessment; respiratory/complex care for recurrent aspiration; GI/ENT/surgery when anatomy or feeding route is relevant; PICU for airway risk.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT: Aspiration precautions, head-of-bed elevation when appropriate, suction plan, oxygen trend, feed-associated symptoms, and secretion burden.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess within 1h after admission and after any feed trial; escalate for apnea, worsening hypoxemia, fatigue, recurrent aspiration, fever with instability, or inability to handle secretions.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Position and suction as needed; titrate oxygen; involve RT for secretion clearance and escalation. Avoid routine deep suctioning when not indicated.

Medications/treatments: Supportive care for chemical pneumonitis; start antibiotics only when bacterial aspiration pneumonia is suspected or symptoms persist/evolve, using local guidance. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Acute respiratory failure
summary: Admit to step-down/PICU; a child needing rapidly escalating oxygen, HFNC/NIV beyond ward capability, recurrent apnea, hypercapnia, exhaustion, or altered mental status should not remain on a routine ward.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to step-down/PICU; a child needing rapidly escalating oxygen, HFNC/NIV beyond ward capability, recurrent apnea, hypercapnia, exhaustion, or altered mental status should not remain on a routine ward.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring; document full vital signs and respiratory assessment at least q15-30 min during escalation, then q1h when stabilized.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry and ECG; frequent work-of-breathing/mental-status assessments; capillary/venous/arterial gas trend when ventilation is impaired; strict intake/output.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Position, suction and oxygen immediately; escalate low-flow to HFNC/NIV per unit protocol. Use bag-mask ventilation for apnea or inadequate ventilation; prepare for intubation before arrest.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs or IV plus IO if unstable; obtain without delaying respiratory stabilization.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO during significant distress or escalation. Use isotonic maintenance cautiously; give 10 mL/kg isotonic boluses only for shock with reassessment because respiratory failure may coexist with cardiac dysfunction.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Blood gas, glucose, electrolytes, CBC and targeted infectious/metabolic studies; lactate and cultures if shock/sepsis; type and screen if invasive procedure likely.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Portable chest radiograph after stabilization when it will identify pneumonia, atelectasis, effusion, pneumothorax, edema, foreign body, or tube position; bedside ultrasound as available.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat the cause immediatelyâ€”bronchodilator/steroid for asthma, antibiotics for bacterial infection, epinephrine for anaphylaxis, diuresis for selected cardiac overload, antidote for toxicologic cause. Avoid sedatives unless airway team is controlling ventilation.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: PICU and RT immediately; anesthesia for anticipated difficult airway/intubation; disease-specific service as indicated.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: One-to-one observation during instability; emergency equipment at bedside; document device, flow/pressure, FiO2, response and events; continuous suction availability.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess within minutes after every support change. Rising CO2, worsening acidosis, reduced effort, deteriorating consciousness, recurrent apnea, or inability to oxygenate/ventilate mandates controlled intubation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Position, suction and oxygen immediately; escalate low-flow to HFNC/NIV per unit protocol. Use bag-mask ventilation for apnea or inadequate ventilation; prepare for intubation before arrest.

title: Bacterial tracheitis / epiglottitis concern
summary: Admit to PICU with anesthesia/ENT involvement; do not place a child with toxic appearance, drooling, tripod posture, severe stridor, poor air entry or rapidly progressive obstruction on a routine ward.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU with anesthesia/ENT involvement; do not place a child with toxic appearance, drooling, tripod posture, severe stridor, poor air entry or rapidly progressive obstruction on a routine ward.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous monitoring with minimal disturbance; q5-15 min during active deterioration.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry/ECG; observe work of breathing, voice, secretions and mental status without forcing an oral examination.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Keep upright with caregiver and provide gentle blow-by oxygen. Do not agitate, force supine positioning, use tongue depressor, or send an unstable child unaccompanied to imaging. Prepare controlled airway in OR/PICU.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain only if it can be done without worsening obstruction; airway control takes priority.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO. Start isotonic IV fluids after safe access; treat shock cautiously with reassessment.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Blood culture, CBC, CRP and airway cultures after airway control; gas only if it will not provoke deterioration.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Do not delay airway management. Neck/chest imaging may be obtained only in a stable child with airway team agreement.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give IV ceftriaxone/cefotaxime plus anti-staphylococcal coverage such as vancomycin for bacterial tracheitis; tailor to cultures/local formulary. Nebulized epinephrine may transiently improve obstruction but is not definitive therapy. Give dexamethasone when upper-airway edema is present per airway team.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Anesthesia, ENT, PICU and RT immediately; ID after stabilization.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Keep child calm, no throat examination, difficult-airway cart and suction at bedside, limit personnel/procedures and document trajectory.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Continuous bedside reassessment. Fatigue, reduced stridor with poor air entry, cyanosis, bradycardia or altered consciousness means imminent complete obstructionâ€”proceed to controlled airway immediately.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Keep upright with caregiver and provide gentle blow-by oxygen. Do not agitate, force supine positioning, use tongue depressor, or send an unstable child unaccompanied to imaging. Prepare controlled airway in OR/PICU.

title: Tracheostomy-dependent child with respiratory deterioration
summary: Admit to a unit capable of the childâ€™s baseline and escalated airway needs; PICU for increased ventilation, recurrent plugging, inability to maintain oxygenation/ventilation, hemodynamic instability or difficult tracheostomy replacement.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to a unit capable of the childâ€™s baseline and escalated airway needs; PICU for increased ventilation, recurrent plugging, inability to maintain oxygenation/ventilation, hemodynamic instability or difficult tracheostomy replacement.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous pulse oximetry during deterioration; q1-2h respiratory assessment initially, then q4h when back near baseline.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Cardiorespiratory monitoring when oxygen/ventilation is above baseline; document trach size/type, baseline settings, oxygen, secretion burden and home airway-clearance regimen.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Follow emergency tracheostomy algorithmâ€”remove speaking valve/cap, suction, check inner cannula/circuit, provide oxygen to face and stoma, and replace blocked/dislodged tube with same size or one size smaller if trained. Bag through trach or face/stoma as appropriate.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain if moderate-severe illness, dehydration or IV therapy is anticipated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Hold feeds during significant distress/aspiration concern; resume home enteral regimen when stable. Use isotonic IV fluids if needed and consider fluid sensitivity in chronic lung/cardiac disease.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Gas, CBC/electrolytes and cultures based on severity. Obtain tracheal aspirate only when lower-airway infection is clinically suspected; interpret chronic colonization cautiously.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph for focal findings, increased support, suspected atelectasis/pneumonia/pneumothorax or tube position concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Reinstitute individualized airway clearance, humidification, bronchodilator and suction plan. Start antibiotics only for clinical bacterial tracheitis/pneumonia using prior cultures and local guidanceâ€”not culture positivity alone.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: RT and senior immediately; PICU/ENT/anesthesia for airway instability; respirology/complex-care team and ID when relevant.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Emergency trach kit at bedside including same-size and one-size-smaller tubes, obturator, suction and bag-mask; caregiver expertise should be actively incorporated.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess after each suction/airway-clearance/support change. Failure to pass suction catheter, sudden loss of end-tidal CO2, rapidly rising pressures, bleeding or recurrent desaturation is an airway emergency.

Bag through trach or face/stoma as appropriate.

title: Sepsis or septic shock
summary: Admit to PICU for shock, vasoactive need, respiratory failure, altered mental status or major organ dysfunction; monitored ward/step-down only after stabilization and when support is within unit capability.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU for shock, vasoactive need, respiratory failure, altered mental status or major organ dysfunction; monitored ward/step-down only after stabilization and when support is within unit capability.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous during resuscitation; BP and perfusion at least q5-15 min until stable, then q1h. Record temperature, capillary refill, pulses, mental status and urine output.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/pulse oximetry; strict intake/output with hourly urine output in shock; serial lactate and organ-function trends; frequent glucose.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen; support ventilation early if work of breathing, encephalopathy or shock is worsening; avoid delaying airway team activation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two large IVs or IV plus IO immediately; obtain cultures but do not delay antibiotics.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO during shock. Give 10-20 mL/kg balanced crystalloid/isotonic saline aliquots with reassessment after each; use smaller aliquots with cardiac/renal disease. Stop boluses for crackles, hepatomegaly, worsening oxygenation or no perfusion benefit and start vasoactive support with PICU.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Blood culture(s), CBC/differential, gas/lactate, glucose, electrolytes, renal/liver tests, coagulation/fibrinogen; urinalysis/culture and source-specific cultures. LP only after stabilization and when safe.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed after initial resuscitationâ€”chest radiograph, ultrasound/CT, echocardiography as indicated; do not delay antibiotics/source control.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics as soon as possibleâ€”within 1 h for septic shock. Choose age/source/device/immunocompromise coverage using local antibiogram; common community regimens use ceftriaxone/cefotaxime, with vancomycin and/or anaerobic/antipseudomonal coverage when indicated. Start epinephrine or norepinephrine infusion for fluid-refractory shock with PICU.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior, PICU and RT immediately for shock; ID for complex source/resistance; surgery/interventional team for source control; hematology for DIC/major cytopenia.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Sepsis timer/checklist, exact antibiotic and fluid times, hourly urine output, repeat perfusion after every bolus, daily weight and line/device review.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess within minutes after each intervention and repeat lactate/organ assessment in 2-4 h. Persistent abnormal perfusion after 40-60 mL/kgâ€”or earlier with fluid intoleranceâ€”requires vasoactive support and PICU.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen; support ventilation early if work of breathing, encephalopathy or shock is worsening; avoid delaying airway team activation.

Medications/treatments: Give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics as soon as possibleâ€”within 1 h for septic shock. Choose age/source/device/immunocompromise coverage using local antibiogram; common community regimens use ceftriaxone/cefotaxime, with vancomycin and/or anaerobic/antipseudomonal coverage when indicated. Start epinephrine or norepinephrine infusion for fluid-refractory shock with PICU.

title: Bacterial meningitis
summary: Admit to PICU for shock, seizures, depressed consciousness, raised-ICP signs, focal deficits or respiratory compromise; otherwise monitored ward care with frequent neurologic observation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU for shock, seizures, depressed consciousness, raised-ICP signs, focal deficits or respiratory compromise; otherwise monitored ward care with frequent neurologic observation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially, then q4h only after stable; continuous monitoring if altered, septic or post-seizure.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry/cardiac monitoring for significant illness; frequent GCS, pupils, focal exam and seizure surveillance; strict intake/output and sodium monitoring.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support as required; avoid hypotension/hypoxemia. Elevate head of bed and keep neck midline if raised ICP is suspected.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs if critically ill; obtain blood cultures but never delay antibiotics for LP or imaging.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO if altered or procedure likely; otherwise age-appropriate diet. Use isotonic fluids and avoid hypotonic maintenance; treat shock with cautious isotonic boluses and reassessment.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Blood culture, CBC, CRP/procalcitonin, glucose, electrolytes/renal/liver tests, coagulation if ill. LP when safe: cell count/differential, protein, glucose with paired serum glucose, Gram stain/culture and molecular testing. Defer LP for instability, focal deficit, papilledema, markedly reduced consciousness or coagulopathy.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Neuroimaging before LP only when clinically indicated; do not routinely image a neurologically intact child and do not delay antibiotics.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start meningitic-dose ceftriaxone or cefotaxime plus vancomycin immediately; add ampicillin for neonates/young infants or Listeria risk. Give dexamethasone with or just before first antibiotic when indicated by local meningitis pathway. Add acyclovir if encephalitis/HSV is possible.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: ID early; PICU for instability/raised ICP/seizure; neurology for seizures/focal findings; public health for meningococcal disease; audiology follow-up after bacterial meningitis.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Droplet precautions for suspected meningococcus/Hib until 24 h of effective therapy; neuro observations; seizure precautions; document antibiotic timing; minimize noxious stimulation if raised ICP concern.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess neurologic and perfusion status at least hourly initially. New bradycardia/hypertension, unequal pupils, focal deficit, repeated seizure, falling sodium or declining GCS requires immediate PICU/raised-ICP management.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support as required; avoid hypotension/hypoxemia. Elevate head of bed and keep neck midline if raised ICP is suspected.

Medications/treatments: Start meningitic-dose ceftriaxone or cefotaxime plus vancomycin immediately; add ampicillin for neonates/young infants or Listeria risk. Give dexamethasone with or just before first antibiotic when indicated by local meningitis pathway. Add acyclovir if encephalitis/HSV is possible.

title: Encephalitis / suspected HSV encephalitis
summary: Admit to PICU for depressed consciousness, recurrent seizures/status, autonomic instability, raised ICP or respiratory compromise; otherwise monitored ward with neurology/ID involvement.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU for depressed consciousness, recurrent seizures/status, autonomic instability, raised ICP or respiratory compromise; otherwise monitored ward with neurology/ID involvement.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially; continuous monitoring if altered or post-seizure; temperature q4h.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Frequent GCS/pupils/focal exam, continuous pulse oximetry/cardiac monitoring, seizure precautions; consider continuous EEG.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/airway support as needed; avoid hypoxia and hypotension; head elevated/neck midline if raised ICP suspected.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain reliable IV access; second line if critically ill.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO until airway/swallow safe; isotonic glucose-containing fluids, avoiding excess free water; strict intake/output and sodium monitoring.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, cultures, glucose, electrolytes, liver/renal tests, ammonia/toxicology/metabolic tests as indicated. LP when safe with cell count, protein/glucose, bacterial culture and viral PCR including HSV; send blood HSV PCR in neonates/young infants or disseminated concern.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: MRI brain preferred when stable; urgent CT for focal deficit, trauma, hemorrhage or raised-ICP concern. Do not delay acyclovir for imaging/LP.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start acyclovir 20 mg/kg IV q8h promptly when HSV is possible (dose/interval adjustment for neonate, renal function and local formulary); provide adequate IV hydration and renal monitoring. Add empiric bacterial meningitis antibiotics until bacterial disease is excluded.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurology and ID urgently; PICU/anesthesia for airway, status or raised ICP; ophthalmology/other services if specific pathogen complications.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Neuro observations and seizure chart; strict urine output; ensure acyclovir is infused and renal dosing reviewed; droplet/contact precautions based on syndrome.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess neuro status at least hourly initially. Worsening GCS, focal signs, repeated seizures, dysautonomia, hyponatremia or rising creatinine requires immediate escalation and treatment adjustment.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/airway support as needed; avoid hypoxia and hypotension; head elevated/neck midline if raised ICP suspected.

Medications/treatments: Start acyclovir 20 mg/kg IV q8h promptly when HSV is possible (dose/interval adjustment for neonate, renal function and local formulary); provide adequate IV hydration and renal monitoring. Add empiric bacterial meningitis antibiotics until bacterial disease is excluded.

title: Fever in a young infant (<=90 days)
summary: Admit all 0-28 day infants receiving empiric antibiotics; admit ill-appearing infants of any age. For well-appearing 29-60 or 61-90 day infants, disposition follows CPS risk stratification, test results, reliable follow-up and local pathway.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit all 0-28 day infants receiving empiric antibiotics; admit ill-appearing infants of any age. For well-appearing 29-60 or 61-90 day infants, disposition follows CPS risk stratification, test results, reliable follow-up and local pathway.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if well and stable; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min assessments if ill, post-bolus, hypothermic, apneic, or receiving respiratory support.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Cardiorespiratory and pulse-ox monitoring for neonates, apnea, hypoxemia or concerning physiology; strict intake/output and feeding documentation.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/suction as needed; escalate for apnea, recurrent desaturation, increased work of breathing or poor perfusion.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for infants requiring parenteral antibiotics, fluids, or full sepsis evaluation; do not delay antibiotics in an ill infant for difficult accessâ€”use IO if necessary.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Breast/formula feeds if well and safe; isotonic glucose-containing IV fluids if intake is poor. Bolus 10-20 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid for shock with reassessment.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: All: urinalysis and urine culture by catheter/SPA. Obtain CBC, blood culture and inflammatory markers according to age/risk pathway. LP is generally required for 0-28 days and any ill/high-risk infant; use age-specific CPS criteria for older well-appearing infants. Send HSV PCR studies when risk features are present.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph only for significant respiratory findings; other imaging source-directed.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start age-appropriate empiric IV antibiotics after cultures without delay. Neonatal regimens commonly include ampicillin plus cefotaxime or gentamicin depending syndrome; add acyclovir 20 mg/kg IV q8h when HSV is suspected and adjust for renal/gestational age. For older infants, ceftriaxone is commonly used when appropriate; verify local pathway.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior for every infant <=28 days and all high-risk infants; PICU for instability/apnea; ID for HSV, meningitis, unusual exposure or resistant organism.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Record rectal temperature, feeding volume, urine output, perfusion and behavior; use neonatal medication/IV-fluid double checks; maintain isolation based on symptoms.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review culture and inflammatory-marker results promptly and reassess at least q2-4h. Any deterioration converts the infant to high risk: full sepsis management, immediate antibiotics and PICU consideration.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/suction as needed; escalate for apnea, recurrent desaturation, increased work of breathing or poor perfusion.

Medications/treatments: Start age-appropriate empiric IV antibiotics after cultures without delay. Neonatal regimens commonly include ampicillin plus cefotaxime or gentamicin depending syndrome; add acyclovir 20 mg/kg IV q8h when HSV is suspected and adjust for renal/gestational age. For older infants, ceftriaxone is commonly used when appropriate; verify local pathway.

title: UTI or pyelonephritis
summary: Admit when toxic or septic, unable to maintain hydration or oral antibiotics, persistent vomiting, significant dehydration, renal impairment, urinary obstruction, known complex uropathy, unreliable follow-up, or age/clinical risk requires inpatient management. Infants under 2â€“3 months require the age-appropriate febrile-infant/sepsis pathway rather than this routine >2-month UTI plan. Escalate to PICU for shock, organ dysfunction, altered mental status, respiratory failure, or rapidly worsening perfusion.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit when toxic or septic, unable to maintain hydration or oral antibiotics, persistent vomiting, significant dehydration, renal impairment, urinary obstruction, known complex uropathy, unreliable follow-up, or age/clinical risk requires inpatient management. Infants under 2â€“3 months require the age-appropriate febrile-infant/sepsis pathway rather than this routine >2-month UTI plan. Escalate to PICU for shock, organ dysfunction, altered mental status, respiratory failure, or rapidly worsening perfusion.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable; q2h initially when moderately unwell. Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring during sepsis, hemodynamic instability, significant electrolyte abnormality, or active fluid resuscitation. Trend fever, blood pressure, heart rate, perfusion, and pain.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Strict intake/output when admitted, dehydrated, young, oliguric, or at risk for AKI. Document urine output and reassess hydration after fluids. Daily weight if ongoing IV fluids, renal dysfunction, or prolonged admission. Review urine culture identification and susceptibilities every day and narrow therapy promptly.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: No routine respiratory support. Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when sepsis, shock, pulmonary edema, or another respiratory process is present.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for parenteral antibiotics, dehydration, vomiting, sepsis, AKI, or inability to tolerate oral therapy. Consider a second IV/IO during shock or difficult resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Encourage oral fluids and regular diet when tolerated. Use isotonic IV fluid for documented dehydration or inadequate intake; reassess after each bolus and avoid automatic repeated boluses in renal/cardiac disease. Use maintenance fluid only for the ongoing deficit in oral intake, and add potassium only after urine output and serum potassium are known.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Before antibiotics when this will not delay treatment: urinalysis and urine culture. Toilet-trained child: clean-catch midstream specimen. Non-toilet-trained child: catheter or suprapubic aspirate for culture. A bag specimen may screen by urinalysis but must not be used to establish the culture diagnosis. Consider CBC, electrolytes, urea/creatinine, CRP and blood culture when toxic, septic, very young, dehydrated, immunocompromised, bacteremia is suspected, renal function is abnormal, or the infection is complicated. Pregnancy testing when clinically applicable.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: No imaging is routinely needed for simple cystitis. For a first febrile UTI in a child under 2 years, arrange renal/bladder ultrasound during the illness or within approximately 2 weeks. Obtain urgent ultrasound when poor urine flow, abdominal/bladder mass, elevated creatinine, known abnormal urinary tract, suspected stone/obstruction/abscess, hemodynamic instability, failure to improve within 24 hours, or fever is not trending down by 48 hours. VCUG is not routine after a first UTI; consider when ultrasound suggests high-grade reflux, selected renal anomalies, or obstructive uropathy.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Obtain urine for urinalysis/culture first when feasible, then start empiric treatment based on age, severity, prior cultures, allergies, renal function, and the current local antibiogram. For children >2 months who are nontoxic and can reliably tolerate oral therapy, common options when locally susceptible include: cefixime 8 mg/kg PO once daily; cephalexin 50 mg/kg/day PO divided q6h; amoxicillin-clavulanate (amoxicillin component, 7:1 formulation) 40 mg/kg/day PO divided q8h; or TMP-SMX 8 mg/kg/day of the trimethoprim component PO divided q12h. For hospitalized/complicated febrile UTI, common parenteral options include ceftriaxone 50â€“75 mg/kg IV/IM q24h (avoid/verify neonatal restrictions), cefotaxime 150 mg/kg/day IV divided q6â€“8h, gentamicin 5â€“7.5 mg/kg IV/IM q24h with renal function/TDM as indicated, or ampicillin 200 mg/kg/day IV divided q6h when organism coverage is appropriate. Cefazolin 100 mg/kg/day IV divided q6â€“8h is another local susceptible-organism option. Select one appropriate regimen rather than combining these automatically. Narrow to culture results. Febrile UTI: usually 7â€“10 total days. Uncomplicated afebrile cystitis in an older child: typically 2â€“4 days using a susceptible oral agent. Do not use nitrofurantoin for suspected pyelonephritis because tissue/serum exposure is inadequate.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Discuss with senior/staff for every admitted young infant, urosepsis, AKI, unusual organism, or uncertain regimen. Consult urology/nephrology for obstruction, stones, abnormal anatomy, poor urine flow, recurrent febrile UTI, renal impairment, or abnormal imaging. Consult ID or antimicrobial stewardship for multidrug resistance, unusual organisms, severe beta-lactam allergy, treatment failure, or limited oral options.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Record collection method and ensure culture was obtained before the first antibiotic when possible. Strict intake/output when ordered; notify for oliguria, hypotension, worsening pain, persistent emesis, poor perfusion, or clinical deterioration. Confirm antibiotic timing, allergy history, renal function, and weight used for dosing.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess perfusion and hydration within 30â€“60 minutes after resuscitation and clinical response within 4â€“6 hours after initial therapy. Review culture at 24â€“48 hours. Failure to improve within 24 hours, fever not trending down by 48 hours, rising creatinine, oliguria, persistent vomiting, or worsening pain should trigger repeat examination, susceptibility review, repeat cultures when indicated, and evaluation for obstruction, abscess, stone, incorrect diagnosis, or resistant organism. Transition IV to oral therapy once clinically improved, afebrile/improving, tolerating oral medication, and an active oral option is available.

treatments.text: Oral hydration when tolerated; isotonic IV replacement/maintenance only when needed. Strict intake/output and renal monitoring in admitted, dehydrated, or complicated cases.

treatments.group: Common oral options (>2 months; verify susceptibility/local pathway)
treatments.text: Cefixime 8 mg/kg PO q24h; cephalexin 50 mg/kg/day PO divided q6h; amoxicillin-clavulanate (amoxicillin component, 7:1 formulation) 40 mg/kg/day PO divided q8h; TMP-SMX 8 mg/kg/day of trimethoprim component PO divided q12h.

treatments.group: Common parenteral options (select one appropriate regimen)
treatments.text: Ceftriaxone 50â€“75 mg/kg IV/IM q24h; cefotaxime 150 mg/kg/day IV divided q6â€“8h; gentamicin 5â€“7.5 mg/kg IV/IM q24h; ampicillin 200 mg/kg/day IV divided q6h when appropriate; cefazolin 100 mg/kg/day IV divided q6â€“8h as a susceptible-organism option. Apply neonatal restrictions and renal/TDM requirements.

title: Cellulitis
summary: Admit to ward for rapidly progressive/extensive cellulitis, systemic illness, failed oral therapy, high-risk location, immunocompromise, inability to take medication or unreliable follow-up; PICU for shock, necrotizing infection or compartment concern.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to ward for rapidly progressive/extensive cellulitis, systemic illness, failed oral therapy, high-risk location, immunocompromise, inability to take medication or unreliable follow-up; PICU for shock, necrotizing infection or compartment concern.

sections.label: Vitals

title: Preseptal cellulitis
summary: Admit if young, systemically unwell, unable to take oral therapy, rapid progression, unreliable follow-up, diagnostic uncertainty, or failure of outpatient therapy; manage as orbital cellulitis if orbital signs cannot be excluded.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit if young, systemically unwell, unable to take oral therapy, rapid progression, unreliable follow-up, diagnostic uncertainty, or failure of outpatient therapy; manage as orbital cellulitis if orbital signs cannot be excluded.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h if febrile/evolving.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Serial eye examâ€”visual behavior/acuity, pupils, ocular movements, pain with movement and proptosis. Pulse oximetry only if clinically indicated.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain if admitted for IV antibiotics, dehydration or uncertain trajectory.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet and oral fluids; isotonic IV fluids if intake poor.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Usually none for mild well child; CBC/CRP and blood culture if febrile, toxic, very young or failing therapy.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Not routine when a reliable normal orbital exam is possible. Contrast imaging if proptosis, restricted/painful movements, reduced vision, RAPD, severe headache, neurologic signs, marked swelling preventing exam, or no response.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: For skin/trauma source use cephalexin PO or cefazolin IV; for sinus/respiratory source use amoxicillin-clavulanate PO or ampicillin-sulbactam IV, adjusted to allergy/MRSA risk and local formulary. Provide analgesia.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior if diagnostic uncertainty; ophthalmology/ENT for any orbital sign, severe swelling, sinus complication or lack of improvement; ID for unusual pathogen/immunocompromise.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None routinely.

title: Orbital cellulitis
summary: Admit to hospital; PICU for sepsis, rapidly progressive swelling, vision compromise, intracranial complication, airway concern or hemodynamic instability.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to hospital; PICU for sepsis, rapidly progressive swelling, vision compromise, intracranial complication, airway concern or hemodynamic instability.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h; q1-2h if toxic/evolving. Document fever and pain trend.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Serial visual acuity when age-appropriate, pupils, colour vision, ocular motility, proptosis and pain with eye movement; continuous monitoring if septic.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Usually none; manage sepsis/airway as required.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Required for IV antibiotics and contrast imaging.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Age-appropriate diet unless surgery/sedation possibleâ€”then NPO per ophthalmology/ENT plan; isotonic IV fluids if poor intake.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, CRP/ESR, blood culture if febrile/toxic; culture operative material if drained.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Contrast CT or MRI of orbits/sinuses urgently for proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, pain with eye movement, decreased vision, RAPD, severe headache, neurologic signs, or inability to examine; include brain/venous imaging if intracranial concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start IV amoxicillin-clavulanate or ceftriaxone/cefotaxime per local formulary; add vancomycin for MRSA risk/severe disease and metronidazole when anaerobic/intracranial coverage is needed. Provide analgesia and nasal/sinus care as directed.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Ophthalmology and ENT urgently; ID for severe/complicated disease; neurosurgery/PICU for intracranial extension, cavernous sinus thrombosis or deterioration.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Mark swelling if useful; perform/document agreed eye observations; no pressure patching; monitor IV antibiotic response and NPO status.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Repeat eye/neuro assessment q2-4h initially. Any decline in vision, new RAPD, worsening motility/proptosis, severe headache, vomiting or neurologic change requires immediate imaging/surgical escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Usually none; manage sepsis/airway as required.

title: Deep neck infection
summary: Admit to CTU/ward only if airway is stable with immediate senior/ENT review; use step-down/PICU when there is drooling, stridor, tripod positioning, trismus with progression, toxic appearance, mediastinal concern, or anticipated difficult airway.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward only if airway is stable with immediate senior/ENT review; use step-down/PICU when there is drooling, stridor, tripod positioning, trismus with progression, toxic appearance, mediastinal concern, or anticipated difficult airway.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially; continuous observation if airway symptoms are present.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry; cardiorespiratory monitoring for airway risk, opioid use, or significant systemic illness. Keep airway equipment immediately available.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Keep the child calm and in a position of comfort; oxygen as tolerated. Do not force an oropharyngeal examination in a child with critical upper-airway signs.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain with experienced staff while minimizing distress; consider anesthetic/ENT support if access attempts may destabilize the airway.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO; isotonic IV fluids with reassessment for dehydration and sepsis.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/differential, CRP, electrolytes, blood culture if febrile/systemically unwell; operative cultures when drained.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Contrast CT neck when stable enough and diagnosis/extent is uncertain; ultrasound for selected superficial disease; never delay airway control for imaging.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start IV antibiotics covering oral flora, streptococci, staphylococci, and anaerobes per hospital pathway; analgesia; corticosteroid only after specialist discussion. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: ENT urgently; anesthesia and PICU early for any airway concern; ID for severe/complicated disease; surgery for mediastinal extension.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Continuous airway observation, suction available, NPO signage, minimal agitation, and documentation of voice, drooling, neck position, swelling, and work of breathing.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess at bedside within 30-60 min and frequently thereafter; call anesthesia/PICU immediately for increasing stridor, fatigue, cyanosis, inability to handle secretions, altered mental status, or rapidly enlarging swelling.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward if true bacteremia is likely, the child is young/high-risk, has an indwelling device, is clinically unwell, cannot ensure follow-up, or needs IV therapy; PICU for sepsis or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h depending on appearance and organism; use sepsis-frequency observations if unstable.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Clinical perfusion, mental status, urine output, fever curve; continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring if unwell.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain reliable access; repeat cultures before antibiotics when feasible, including each central-line lumen if present.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet if stable; isotonic IV fluids only for poor intake or perfusion deficit.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat blood culture, CBC/differential, renal/liver function and source-directed tests; inflammatory markers if useful for trend. Confirm organism, time to positivity, number of positive bottles, and contamination likelihood.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed imaging only; consider echocardiography for selected organisms, persistent bacteremia, cardiac risk, or endocarditis concern after specialist review.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give organism- and source-appropriate empiric IV antibiotics after repeat cultures; narrow promptly when identification/susceptibility is known. Verify doses and allergies.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: ID for S. aureus, fungal infection, persistent bacteremia, unusual organisms, hardware, endovascular concern, or uncertainty; relevant surgical service for source control.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Document exact culture details, antibiotic administration, line findings, fever, perfusion, urine output, and repeat-culture timing.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess within 1h after arrival/therapy and review microbiology actively overnight; escalate for persistent positive cultures, shock, focal neurologic signs, new murmur, embolic findings, or device infection.

title: Kawasaki disease
summary: Admit to CTU/ward with early cardiology/rheumatology or local KD-team involvement; PICU for shock, myocardial dysfunction, significant arrhythmia, or severe systemic inflammation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward with early cardiology/rheumatology or local KD-team involvement; PICU for shock, myocardial dysfunction, significant arrhythmia, or severe systemic inflammation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q1-2h for shock features, tachycardia out of proportion, or cardiac dysfunction.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, daily weight, perfusion, fever curve; cardiorespiratory monitoring if myocardial involvement, shock, or arrhythmia concern.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as indicated; assess for pulmonary edema or pleural effusions in severe disease.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access before immunomodulatory therapy; consider additional access if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet as tolerated; cautious isotonic fluids if dehydrated, with reassessment for myocardial dysfunction and third spacing.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/differential, CRP/ESR, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, albumin, urinalysis; blood/urine cultures and additional infectious evaluation as indicated; cardiac biomarkers if myocardial involvement suspected.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: ECG and echocardiogram per KD pathway; chest imaging only if respiratory/cardiac findings warrant it.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: After cardiology/senior review give IVIG 2 g/kg once plus aspirin according to current CPS/local pathway; treat ideally within 10 days of fever and later if persistent inflammation/coronary disease. sections.text: Consults: Cardiology early; rheumatology/ID according to local model; PICU for shock or cardiac dysfunction.

sections.text: Nursing: Record exact fever times, mucocutaneous findings, perfusion, intake/output, infusion reactions, and aspirin/antiplatelet precautions.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess during and after IVIG and at least q4h; urgent escalation for hypotension, gallop rhythm, respiratory distress, chest pain, arrhythmia, altered mental status, or persistent/recurrent fever after treatment window.

summary: Admit to ward for hypoxemia, dehydration, significant comorbidity, bacterial coinfection, encephalopathy, myositis/rhabdomyolysis or inability to maintain care; PICU for respiratory failure, shock, myocarditis or severe neurologic disease.

sections.text: Admit to ward for hypoxemia, dehydration, significant comorbidity, bacterial coinfection, encephalopathy, myositis/rhabdomyolysis or inability to maintain care; PICU for respiratory failure, shock, myocarditis or severe neurologic disease.

sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h based on severity; continuous monitoring while oxygen-dependent or significantly ill.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Respiratory status, hydration/urine output, mental status and muscle pain/weakness; cardiac monitoring for myocarditis/electrolyte abnormalities.

sections.label: Respiratory support

sections.label: Fluids / diet

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Viral PCR if it changes management/isolation; CBC, electrolytes/renal tests, CK/urinalysis for myositis, cultures and inflammatory markers for bacterial coinfection, troponin/BNP if cardiac concern.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph for hypoxemia/focal findings/complication; cardiac/neuro imaging as indicated.

sections.label: Medications / treatment

sections.text: Consults: PICU for escalating support; ID for severe/antiviral resistance/immunocompromise; cardiology, neurology or nephrology for complications.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Droplet/contact precautions per infection control; fever/pain control, hydration and urine-colour monitoring; document oxygen trajectory.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess q2-4h and after support changes. Rapid oxygen escalation, hemoptysis, shock, altered mental status, severe muscle pain with dark urine or cardiac signs requires complication-specific escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen, suction and escalation to HFNC/NIV per unit protocol; early PICU for rapid progression.
