title: Invasive group A streptococcal infection / toxic shock
summary: Admit to PICU for shock, organ dysfunction, necrotizing infection or toxin-mediated disease; stable bacteremia without shock still requires close monitored care and source evaluation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU for shock, organ dysfunction, necrotizing infection or toxin-mediated disease; stable bacteremia without shock still requires close monitored care and source evaluation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous; BP/perfusion q5-15 min during resuscitation, then q1h.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/pulse oximetry, hourly urine output, serial lactate, coagulation, renal/liver function and CK when myositis/necrotizing disease is possible.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen and early ventilatory support for respiratory failure; prepare for perioperative airway if source control is needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs/IO; arterial/central access with PICU as indicated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO. Balanced crystalloid 10-20 mL/kg aliquots with reassessment; move early to vasoactive support if fluid-refractory or fluid intolerant.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Blood and source cultures, CBC, gas/lactate, electrolytes, renal/liver tests, CK, coagulation/fibrinogen and type/crossmatch; repeat frequently.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed imaging only if it does not delay surgery; bedside assessment and operative exploration take priority for necrotizing infection.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give broad empiric sepsis coverage immediately, including a beta-lactam active against GAS plus clindamycin for toxin suppression; add MRSA/gram-negative/anaerobic coverage until source defined. Consider IVIG for refractory streptococcal toxic shock with ID/PICU. Urgent surgical debridement/source control is essential.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: PICU, ID and surgery immediately; hematology/transfusion medicine for DIC/IVIG considerations.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Sepsis checklist, exact antibiotic/fluid/vasoactive times, mark skin changes, hourly urine output and preparation for repeated OR assessment.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess within minutes. Pain out of proportion, rapidly spreading edema/erythema, bullae, anesthesia, rising lactate/CK or persistent shock mandates immediate operative exploration and escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen and early ventilatory support for respiratory failure; prepare for perioperative airway if source control is needed.

title: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
summary: Admit to the hospital DKA pathway; PICU/step-down for severe DKA, cerebral-injury risk, hemodynamic instability, altered mental status, very young child, major electrolyte abnormality, or monitoring needs beyond the ward.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to the hospital DKA pathway; PICU/step-down for severe DKA, cerebral-injury risk, hemodynamic instability, altered mental status, very young child, major electrolyte abnormality, or monitoring needs beyond the ward.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1h with neurologic assessment throughout insulin therapy; temperature q4h; weight on admission and use the measured weight for calculations.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring and pulse oximetry; hourly glucose and neurologic checks; strict intake/output; document corrected sodium, fluid balance and Glasgow Coma Scale trend.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen only if needed; avoid routine bicarbonate. If consciousness declines, protect airway with PICU/anesthesia while avoiding hypocapnia from excessive ventilation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs if possible; do not delay initial fluid for a second line. Avoid central line unless necessary because of thrombosis risk.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO initially except ice chips if vomiting/altered. Give 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid 10-20 mL/kg over 20-30 min; additional 10 mL/kg boluses for shock with reassessment. Replace maintenance plus deficit over ~36 h per protocol; add dextrose when glucose falls to ~15-17 mmol/L or earlier if falling rapidly.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Initial glucose, VBG, sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate, urea/creatinine, calcium, magnesium, phosphate, beta-hydroxybutyrate/ketones, osmolality if indicated; repeat glucose hourly and electrolytes/gas q2-4h per severity.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely. Neuroimaging must not delay treatment of suspected cerebral injury.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start regular insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 units/kg/h after at least 1 h of fluids; no insulin bolus. Add potassium to IV fluids once urine output/renal function and serum potassium permit. For suspected cerebral injury give 3% saline 5 mL/kg over 10-15 min (max 250 mL) or mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg promptly and call PICU.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology early; PICU immediately for severe DKA, cerebral-injury signs, shock, refractory acidosis/electrolytes, or need for airway support; pharmacy for two-bag/insulin setup.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Use a DKA flowsheet; independent double-check insulin and fluids; hourly neuro/glucose documentation; do not give insulin bolus or bicarbonate without specialist direction.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review hourly glucose fall, sodium trend, perfusion and neuro status; adjust dextrose rather than stopping insulin. Headache, irritability, bradycardia, hypertension, vomiting, cranial nerve change or declining GCS = treat cerebral injury immediately.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen only if needed; avoid routine bicarbonate. If consciousness declines, protect airway with PICU/anesthesia while avoiding hypocapnia from excessive ventilation.

Medications/treatments: Start regular insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 units/kg/h after at least 1 h of fluids; no insulin bolus. Add potassium to IV fluids once urine output/renal function and serum potassium permit. For suspected cerebral injury give 3% saline 5 mL/kg over 10-15 min (max 250 mL) or mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg promptly and call PICU.

title: New-onset diabetes without DKA
summary: Admit to endocrinology/CTU when education cannot be completed safely as an outpatient, there is dehydration/ketosis, social or safeguarding concern, very young age, significant comorbidity, or unreliable follow-up; PICU only if DKA or critical metabolic instability develops.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to endocrinology/CTU when education cannot be completed safely as an outpatient, there is dehydration/ketosis, social or safeguarding concern, very young age, significant comorbidity, or unreliable follow-up; PICU only if DKA or critical metabolic instability develops.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h when stable; increase frequency for dehydration, vomiting, or evolving ketosis.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bedside glucose before meals, bedtime, overnight, and as symptoms dictate; ketones until cleared; strict I&O and daily weight.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Not routinely required; assess for Kussmaul breathing or altered mental status suggesting evolving DKA.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Not routinely required if drinking and not acidotic; obtain if dehydrated, vomiting, or labs/IV therapy are needed.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Encourage sugar-free fluids and regular carbohydrate-consistent meals per diabetes team; isotonic IV fluids for dehydration without using a DKA protocol unless criteria are met.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Confirm serum glucose, electrolytes, bicarbonate/venous gas, beta-hydroxybutyrate or ketones; HbA1c and diabetes classification labs per endocrinology; screen for associated autoimmune disease per pathway.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start subcutaneous insulin regimen with endocrinology using weight/age/puberty considerations; hypoglycemia orders and sick-day plan; verify all insulin doses independently.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology/diabetes educator, dietitian, nursing education, social work as needed.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Double-check insulin, carbohydrate intake, glucose/ketone documentation, injection teaching, device education, and hypoglycemia supplies.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess glucose/ketones after insulin and meals; convert immediately to DKA pathway and call senior/endocrinology if acidosis, persistent vomiting, rising ketones, worsening dehydration, or altered mental status appears.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Not routinely required; assess for Kussmaul breathing or altered mental status suggesting evolving DKA.
Medications/treatments: Start subcutaneous insulin regimen with endocrinology using weight/age/puberty considerations; hypoglycemia orders and sick-day plan; verify all insulin doses independently.

title: Hypoglycemia
summary: Admit to ward for recurrent/persistent hypoglycemia, inability to maintain glucose orally, suspected endocrine/metabolic disease, toxic ingestion, liver disease, or need for continuous dextrose; PICU for seizures, coma, high glucose-infusion requirement, or instability.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to ward for recurrent/persistent hypoglycemia, inability to maintain glucose orally, suspected endocrine/metabolic disease, toxic ingestion, liver disease, or need for continuous dextrose; PICU for seizures, coma, high glucose-infusion requirement, or instability.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h when stable; q15-30 min during severe symptoms/resuscitation. Obtain an accurate weight.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bedside glucose every 15 min until corrected, then q30-60 min until stable and before feeds/overnight as directed; continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring if symptomatic or on high-concentration dextrose.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: ABC stabilization; oxygen and seizure management as required.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain promptly for symptomatic/severe or recurrent hypoglycemia; IO if unstable. Central access may be needed for high dextrose concentration.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: If awake and safe, give rapid oral carbohydrate followed by complex carbohydrate/feed. If unable to take orally, give IV dextrose and continue glucose-containing isotonic fluids titrated to maintain target glucose.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Before treatment if this causes no delay, obtain critical sample at plasma glucose <=2.8 mmol/L: laboratory glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, free fatty acids, cortisol, growth hormone, lactate, ammonia, electrolytes, liver tests, acylcarnitine profile and urine organic acids/toxicology as indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely; targeted imaging only for suspected intracranial, hepatic, adrenal or ingestion-related cause.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat immediately. Common IV rescue is D10W 2-5 mL/kg (institution/age dependent), then glucose infusion adjusted to response. If no IV, glucagon IM/SC may be used according to age/weight and available product. For neonates, 40% dextrose gel 0.5 mL/kg buccally may be used with a feed when appropriate.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology/metabolic genetics for unexplained, ketotic/non-ketotic recurrent hypoglycemia or high glucose requirement; toxicology for ingestion; PICU for neurologic compromise or escalating dextrose.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Treat based on bedside result but send confirmatory laboratory glucose; document symptoms, treatment, feeding and response; never leave an infant/child fasting without a glucose plan.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Recheck in 15 min after each rescue. Repeat rescue/escalate infusion if still low. Inability to maintain target despite glucose infusion, absent ketones, hepatomegaly, acidosis, hyperammonemia or recurrent overnight lows requires urgent specialist review.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: ABC stabilization; oxygen and seizure management as required.

Medications/treatments: Treat immediately. Common IV rescue is D10W 2-5 mL/kg (institution/age dependent), then glucose infusion adjusted to response. If no IV, glucagon IM/SC may be used according to age/weight and available product. For neonates, 40% dextrose gel 0.5 mL/kg buccally may be used with a feed when appropriate.

title: Adrenal crisis
summary: Admit to step-down/PICU if shock, severe electrolyte disturbance, altered mental status or repeated hypoglycemia; otherwise monitored ward care after stabilization.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to step-down/PICU if shock, severe electrolyte disturbance, altered mental status or repeated hypoglycemia; otherwise monitored ward care after stabilization.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q15-30 min during resuscitation, then q1-2h until stable and q4h thereafter; weight for dosing.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring for shock/hyperkalemia; frequent glucose, neurologic/perfusion assessment and strict intake/output.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support as required; altered mental status may reflect shock, hypoglycemia or severe sodium disturbance.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs or IO immediately if unstable; do not delay hydrocortisone for testing or access difficulty.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Give 0.9% saline 20 mL/kg rapidly for shock (smaller aliquots if cardiac/renal concern), repeat to perfusion; add dextrose for hypoglycemia and continue isotonic glucose-containing maintenance/deficit fluids.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Draw cortisol and ACTH before steroid only if this will not delay treatment; glucose, electrolytes, gas, urea/creatinine, CBC and cultures if infection suspected. Repeat sodium, potassium and glucose frequently.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely; investigate precipitating illness as indicated.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Hydrocortisone 100 mg/m2 IV/IM immediately (max 100 mg); practical emergency doses: infant 25 mg, child <15 kg 50 mg, child >=15 kg 100 mg. Continue 30-50 mg/m2/day divided q6h IV (or q8h IM) and taper with endocrinology once stable.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology urgently; PICU for shock, severe electrolyte disturbance or neurologic compromise; infectious disease/other services for precipitating illness.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Give steroid before nonessential investigations; document emergency dose/time; maintain stress-dose plan and medical-alert information; monitor for fluid overload and potassium change.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess perfusion and glucose within 10-15 min, electrolytes within 1-2 h. Persistent shock after fluids/hydrocortisone requires PICU, vasoactive support and search for sepsis/hemorrhage.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support as required; altered mental status may reflect shock, hypoglycemia or severe sodium disturbance.

Medications/treatments: Hydrocortisone 100 mg/m2 IV/IM immediately (max 100 mg); practical emergency doses: infant 25 mg, child <15 kg 50 mg, child >=15 kg 100 mg. Continue 30-50 mg/m2/day divided q6h IV (or q8h IM) and taper with endocrinology once stable.

title: Hyponatremia / SIADH
summary: Admit to CTU/ward for symptomatic, moderate/severe, rapidly falling, or etiologically unclear hyponatremia; PICU for seizure, altered mental status, respiratory compromise, severe symptoms, or need for hypertonic saline infusion.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward for symptomatic, moderate/severe, rapidly falling, or etiologically unclear hyponatremia; PICU for seizure, altered mental status, respiratory compromise, severe symptoms, or need for hypertonic saline infusion.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h when stable; continuous observation during acute correction or neurologic symptoms.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, daily weight, neurologic checks, and fluid balance; continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring for severe/symptomatic cases.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation during seizure or encephalopathy; avoid free water.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; two lines if severe symptoms or hypertonic therapy is anticipated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Stop hypotonic fluids. Use isotonic maintenance for most hospitalized children when appropriate; fluid restrict for SIADH after volume status is established; treat hypovolemia carefully.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat serum sodium at a frequency matched to severity/correction; serum osmolality, glucose, urea/creatinine, urine sodium/osmolality, and cause-directed endocrine/renal tests.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Cause-directed only; neuroimaging if focal deficits, trauma, suspected CNS pathology, or unexplained severe symptoms.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Symptomatic severe hyponatremia requires hypertonic saline per emergency/PICU pathway; treat the underlying cause and prevent overly rapid correction. Verify concentration and calculations with pharmacy.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: PICU for symptoms/severe level; nephrology/endocrinology for complex, recurrent, renal, or endocrine causes; neurology if seizures/CNS disease.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Exact intake/output, no unapproved free water, double-check fluid sodium concentration/rate, and draw timed sodium levels.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess neurologic status and sodium closely during correction; escalate for seizure, declining GCS, respiratory change, rising sodium faster than target, or inability to control fluid balance.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation during seizure or encephalopathy; avoid free water.

Medications/treatments: Symptomatic severe hyponatremia requires hypertonic saline per emergency/PICU pathway; treat the underlying cause and prevent overly rapid correction. Verify concentration and calculations with pharmacy.

title: Hypernatremia
summary: Admit to CTU/ward for significant hypernatremia, dehydration, neurologic symptoms, unreliable enteral replacement, or uncertain chronicity; PICU for severe symptoms, shock, seizures, or need for very frequent laboratory correction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward for significant hypernatremia, dehydration, neurologic symptoms, unreliable enteral replacement, or uncertain chronicity; PICU for severe symptoms, shock, seizures, or need for very frequent laboratory correction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h; more frequently if shock, neurologic symptoms, or active rapid changes.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, daily or more frequent weight, neurologic checks, and careful cumulative fluid balance; cardiorespiratory monitoring if severe.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support as indicated; seizure precautions for severe hypernatremia.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; consider second access if shock or frequent sampling is needed.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Restore intravascular volume first with isotonic fluid when shocked, then replace free-water deficit gradually using a calculated plan; include ongoing losses and avoid overly rapid correction.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Serial sodium, glucose, urea/creatinine, potassium, bicarbonate, osmolality; urine studies and endocrine/renal testing when diabetes insipidus or renal loss is possible.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Cause-directed only; neuroimaging for focal findings, trauma, or unexplained severe neurologic symptoms.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat the cause, replace deficits gradually, and correct concurrent glucose/electrolyte abnormalities; verify calculations and fluid composition with senior/pharmacy.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology/endocrinology for severe, recurrent, DI-related, renal, or complex cases; PICU for neurologic symptoms or shock.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Accurate hourly intake/output in severe cases, timed weights/labs, and independent double-check of fluid composition/rate.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess sodium trend and neurologic status at each laboratory interval; escalate for seizure, cerebral edema concern, worsening shock, oliguria, or correction outside the planned rate.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support as indicated; seizure precautions for severe hypernatremia.
Medications/treatments: Treat the cause, replace deficits gradually, and correct concurrent glucose/electrolyte abnormalities; verify calculations and fluid composition with senior/pharmacy.

title: Hyperkalemia
summary: Admit to monitored CTU/step-down; PICU for ECG changes, severe elevation, rapid rise, renal failure with oliguria/anuria, hemodynamic instability, or need for repeated temporizing therapy/dialysis.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored CTU/step-down; PICU for ECG changes, severe elevation, rapid rise, renal failure with oliguria/anuria, hemodynamic instability, or need for repeated temporizing therapy/dialysis.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h until potassium and ECG are stable, then space cautiously.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring; strict I&O; repeat ECG after treatment or any rhythm change.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: As needed; prepare resuscitation equipment if ECG changes or instability are present.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Immediate reliable IV access; second line if severe. Confirm a non-hemolyzed sample without delaying treatment when ECG changes are present.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Stop potassium-containing fluids/feeds and offending medications; manage volume status and glucose carefully.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat potassium, glucose, blood gas/bicarbonate, calcium, magnesium, phosphate, urea/creatinine; CK/uric acid and hemolysis/tumor-lysis studies when indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Not routinely required; renal ultrasound for obstruction or selected renal causes.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Stop potassium sources. With ECG change or severe hyperkalemia give calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV (max 10 mL) with monitoring; shift potassium with regular insulin 0.1 units/kg IV plus dextrose, nebulized salbutamol and bicarbonate only for significant acidosis. Remove potassium with diuretic/resin/dialysis as appropriate; use local emergency protocol and pharmacy double check.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology urgently for renal failure, refractory hyperkalemia, or dialysis concern; PICU for ECG changes/instability; oncology if tumor lysis.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Continuous rhythm observation, immediate reporting of ECG changes, frequent glucose checks after insulin-based therapy, strict I&O, and timed repeat potassium.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess ECG and potassium within the pathway-defined interval after each intervention; escalate for bradycardia, QRS widening, ventricular arrhythmia, recurrent rise, hypoglycemia, or oliguria/anuria.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: As needed; prepare resuscitation equipment if ECG changes or instability are present.

Medications/treatments: Stop potassium sources. With ECG change or severe hyperkalemia give calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV (max 10 mL) with monitoring; shift potassium with regular insulin 0.1 units/kg IV plus dextrose, nebulized salbutamol and bicarbonate only for significant acidosis. Remove potassium with diuretic/resin/dialysis as appropriate; use local emergency protocol and pharmacy double check.

title: Hypocalcemia
summary: Admit to CTU/ward for symptomatic or significant hypocalcemia, prolonged QT, seizure/tetany, or unclear cause; PICU for arrhythmia, airway compromise, recurrent seizure, or continuous IV calcium requirement.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward for symptomatic or significant hypocalcemia, prolonged QT, seizure/tetany, or unclear cause; PICU for arrhythmia, airway compromise, recurrent seizure, or continuous IV calcium requirement.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h; continuous observation during IV replacement.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Cardiac monitoring for symptomatic disease or IV calcium; seizure precautions and neurologic checks; strict I&O when renal disease is possible.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation during seizure, laryngospasm, or severe tetany.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; verify patency carefully for IV calcium because extravasation can cause injury.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet if safe; correct associated magnesium deficiency and address phosphate/vitamin D intake according to cause.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Ionized and total calcium, albumin, magnesium, phosphate, PTH, vitamin D, renal function, blood gas; ECG and cause-directed tests.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Cause-directed only; consider skeletal imaging for rickets or renal imaging when indicated.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Symptomatic/severe hypocalcemia: calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV slowly (max 10-20 mL per local protocol) with ECG and secure IV-site monitoring; correct magnesium and cause. sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology for unclear/recurrent disease; nephrology for renal causes; cardiology for persistent QT/arrhythmia; genetics if syndromic concern.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Cardiac monitoring, IV-site checks during calcium infusion, seizure precautions, and timed repeat ionized calcium/magnesium.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess symptoms, ECG, and ionized calcium after treatment; escalate for laryngospasm, seizure, ventricular arrhythmia, refractory low calcium, or infusion extravasation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation during seizure, laryngospasm, or severe tetany.

Medications/treatments: Symptomatic/severe hypocalcemia: calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV slowly (max 10-20 mL per local protocol) with ECG and secure IV-site monitoring; correct magnesium and cause. Oral calcium/calcitriol for stable cases with endocrinology/nephrology guidance.

title: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
summary: Admit for significant mucosal bleeding, severe headache/neuro symptoms, hemodynamic concern, inability to ensure follow-up, diagnostic uncertainty or treatment requiring observation; isolated skin findings with well child are often outpatient after hematology discussion.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit for significant mucosal bleeding, severe headache/neuro symptoms, hemodynamic concern, inability to ensure follow-up, diagnostic uncertainty or treatment requiring observation; isolated skin findings with well child are often outpatient after hematology discussion.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring

sections.text: Admit directly to PICU/oncology-capable monitored setting for WBC >=100 x10^9/L with suspected leukemia or any respiratory, neurologic, visual, renal or priapism symptoms; avoid routine ward placement.

sections.text: Vitals: Continuous monitoring; q1h neurologic, respiratory and perfusion assessments initially.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/pulse oximetry, strict intake/output, daily weights; serial tumor-lysis labs q4-6h or more frequently when unstable.

sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen as needed; avoid unnecessary sedation/intubation in a possible anterior mediastinal massâ€”call anesthesia/PICU/oncology before airway intervention whenever possible.

sections.text: IV access: Two peripheral IVs; avoid central line/procedural sedation until mediastinal mass and coagulopathy are assessed. Do not delay treatment if access is difficult.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Begin carefully monitored isotonic hydration for tumor-lysis prevention unless fluid overloaded; avoid potassium/phosphate-containing fluids initially. Avoid red-cell transfusion before hematology review because viscosity may worsen leukostasis.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat CBC/differential and urgent manual smear, electrolytes, creatinine, uric acid, phosphate, calcium, LDH, coagulation/fibrinogen, type and screen; blood gas/lactate if unstable.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent chest radiograph before sedation/central access to assess mediastinal mass; neuroimaging only for symptoms and after stabilization.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start tumor-lysis prophylaxis/treatment with hematologyâ€”rasburicase for high risk/raised uric acid or allopurinol for selected lower risk. sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology/oncology and PICU immediately; anesthesia if airway/procedure; nephrology for severe tumor lysis/renal failure.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Minimize exertion, maintain accurate fluid balance, avoid potassium/phosphate supplementation and nonessential transfusion, institute tumor-lysis lab schedule and bleeding precautions.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess neuro/respiratory status hourly. New headache, confusion, focal deficit, hypoxemia, chest pain, priapism, oliguria or rising potassium/phosphate/uric acid requires immediate cytoreduction/PICU response.

sections.label: Imaging

sections.label: Medications / treatment

sections.label: Consults

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Mark/measure spleen edge, document perfusion and transfusion response, monitor for reaction, and avoid delay in blood administration once ordered.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency

sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if stable; more frequently with active bleeding or after major trauma.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bleeding site, neurovascular status, pain, circumference/swelling, urine/stool, neurologic checks after head injury; cardiorespiratory monitoring if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, type and screen, PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen and factor/inhibitor testing as directed. Normal coagulation tests do not exclude every bleeding disorder.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Immediate CT for significant head injury/symptoms after factor is started; ultrasound/MRI for selected muscle/joint bleeds; source-directed imaging.

sections.label: Medications / treatment

sections.label: Consults

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency

title: Tumor lysis syndrome
summary: Admit to oncology with monitored/step-down capability; PICU for arrhythmia, severe electrolyte disturbance, oliguria/anuria, seizure, fluid overload, or anticipated renal replacement therapy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to oncology with monitored/step-down capability; PICU for arrhythmia, severe electrolyte disturbance, oliguria/anuria, seizure, fluid overload, or anticipated renal replacement therapy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h during active instability, then q2-4h once controlled.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring, strict hourly I&O, frequent weights, fluid balance, neurologic status, and signs of pulmonary edema.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; avoid fluid overload and prepare for escalation if pulmonary edema develops.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable access, often two lines; central access only with oncology plan and procedural safety review.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Start oncology-directed IV hydration; avoid potassium/phosphate-containing fluids and unnecessary calcium; adjust for cardiac/renal status.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Frequent potassium, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, creatinine, glucose, bicarbonate, LDH, magnesium; ECG and urinalysis. Frequency is based on TLS risk and active abnormalities.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Not routinely required; renal ultrasound if obstruction is suspected; chest imaging for pulmonary edema/mediastinal mass concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Uric-acid lowering therapy and electrolyte treatment per oncology/TLS pathway; treat hyperkalemia emergently; avoid routine calcium for asymptomatic hypocalcemia with high phosphate. Verify doses and G6PD considerations.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Oncology and nephrology immediately; PICU early; cardiology for significant arrhythmia.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Hourly urine output, continuous rhythm observation, independent fluid/medication checks, and exact timing of repeat TLS labs.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess at each lab interval; escalate for rising potassium/phosphate/creatinine, falling calcium with symptoms, arrhythmia, seizure, oliguria, or fluid overload.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; avoid fluid overload and prepare for escalation if pulmonary edema develops.

sections.text: Admit to monitored ward for confirmed symptomatic DVT/PE requiring anticoagulation; PICU for hemodynamic instability, significant hypoxemia, massive PE, intracranial thrombosis with deterioration or high bleeding risk.

sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if stable; continuous monitoring for PE or unstable thrombosis.

sections.text: Monitoring: Bleeding checks, neurovascular/limb assessment, oxygenation and strict intake/output when renal disease affects anticoagulation.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and cardiopulmonary support for PE; avoid unnecessary ambulation in unstable PE but routine bed rest is not required for stable DVT.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for therapy/labs; avoid repeated traumatic procedures once anticoagulated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet; hydration appropriate to condition; NPO only if intervention planned.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/platelets, PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, renal/liver function, pregnancy test when applicable; anti-Xa or aPTT monitoring according to agent. Thrombophilia tests should be hematology-directed and timed appropriately.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Compression ultrasound for limb DVT; CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q imaging for PE based on stability/renal function; MRV/CTV for cerebral venous thrombosis.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start LMWH or unfractionated heparin using weight-based local anticoagulation protocol after bleeding-risk review. Thrombolysis/thrombectomy is reserved for selected life-/limb-threatening thrombosis with hematology/PICU/interventional team.

title: Acute transfusion reaction
summary: Admit/transfer to monitored setting based on severity; PICU for shock, respiratory failure, hemolysis, anaphylaxis, TRALI, severe TACO or DIC.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit/transfer to monitored setting based on severity; PICU for shock, respiratory failure, hemolysis, anaphylaxis, TRALI, severe TACO or DIC.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Stop transfusion and obtain full vitals immediately; q5-15 min until stable, then q1-4h according to reaction.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/pulse oximetry for moderate-severe reaction; strict intake/output; monitor urine colour and fluid status.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support; manage anaphylaxis with IM epinephrine; ventilatory support for TRALI; upright position/diuresis for TACO when appropriate.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Keep line open with new tubing and 0.9% saline; do not restart the implicated product. Obtain additional access if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Treat shock with cautious isotonic boluses; avoid excess fluid in TACO. Regular diet when stable.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Notify blood bank immediately. Send post-reaction blood sample and implicated bag/tubing per protocol; CBC, DAT, bilirubin, LDH, haptoglobin, plasma/urine hemoglobin, renal tests, coagulation and cultures if septic reaction suspected.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph for dyspnea/hypoxemia to assess edema/TRALI; other imaging source-directed.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treatment depends on phenotypeâ€”IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis, antipyretic for febrile nonhemolytic reaction after serious causes excluded, antibiotics for septic reaction, diuretic for TACO. Do not give antihistamine as a substitute for epinephrine.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Transfusion medicine/blood bank for every suspected reaction; hematology and PICU for severe reaction; ID for contaminated product/sepsis.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Stop product, verify patient/unit identifiers, maintain IV with new saline tubing, preserve bag/tubing, document symptoms and exact times; complete reaction form.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess within minutes and trend hemolysis/renal/respiratory parameters. Worsening hypoxemia, hypotension, hemoglobinuria, oliguria or bleeding requires immediate PICU and reaction-specific treatment.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support; manage anaphylaxis with IM epinephrine; ventilatory support for TRALI; upright position/diuresis for TACO when appropriate.

Medications/treatments: Treatment depends on phenotypeâ€”IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis, antipyretic for febrile nonhemolytic reaction after serious causes excluded, antibiotics for septic reaction, diuretic for TACO. Do not give antihistamine as a substitute for epinephrine.

title: Status epilepticus
summary: Admit to PICU/step-down after convulsive status, repeated rescue medication, respiratory compromise, persistent altered mental status, or second-line antiseizure therapy; selected rapidly recovered patients may be managed on a monitored ward with neurology agreement.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU/step-down after convulsive status, repeated rescue medication, respiratory compromise, persistent altered mental status, or second-line antiseizure therapy; selected rapidly recovered patients may be managed on a monitored ward with neurology agreement.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous during active seizure; q15 min after rescue until stable, then q1-2h. Record seizure start, medication times and measured weight/estimated weight.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG, pulse oximetry and cardiorespiratory monitoring; bedside glucose immediately; frequent GCS/pupil/neuro checks; consider continuous EEG for persistent encephalopathy or suspected nonconvulsive status.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Position, suction, high-flow oxygen and bag-mask ventilation if needed; prepare for intubation after repeated benzodiazepines or refractory seizure, with PICU/anesthesia.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV/IO promptly, but do not delay first-line intranasal/buccal/IM benzodiazepine while obtaining access.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO until awake and swallow-safe; isotonic maintenance if needed. Correct hypoglycemia and clinically important electrolyte derangements promptly.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose, electrolytes including calcium/magnesium, gas, CBC and antiseizure drug levels when relevant; toxicology, cultures/LP and metabolic studies based on cause. Pregnancy test when applicable.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent CT for trauma, focal deficit, concern for hemorrhage/raised ICP or no recovery; MRI when stable for unexplained/focal status. Imaging must not delay seizure termination.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: First line: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IN/IM/buccal (max 10 mg; max 5 mg per nostril), repeat once after 5 min if required. If still seizing, give one second-line load: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1000 mg PE), or phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV (max 1000 mg), per local algorithm.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurology and senior immediately; PICU/anesthesia for second-line therapy, respiratory depression, refractory seizure or persistent coma; ID for CNS infection concern; toxicology for ingestion.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Seizure precautions, oxygen/suction at bedside, no objects in mouth, document semiology and exact duration, independent medication double-check, monitor BP/respiration after each dose.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Assess at 5 min after each benzodiazepine and during second-line infusion. Ongoing seizure after adequate benzodiazepine plus second-line agent is refractory statusâ€”activate PICU/anesthesia and continuous-infusion pathway.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Position, suction, high-flow oxygen and bag-mask ventilation if needed; prepare for intubation after repeated benzodiazepines or refractory seizure, with PICU/anesthesia.

Medications/treatments: First line: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IN/IM/buccal (max 10 mg; max 5 mg per nostril), repeat once after 5 min if required. If still seizing, give one second-line load: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1000 mg PE), or phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV (max 1000 mg), per local algorithm.

sections.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; procedural sedation support as required.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain IV before reduction, especially with dehydration, significant pain, vomiting or possible surgery.

sections.label: Fluids / diet

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, electrolytes, glucose and type/screen if ill, prolonged symptoms, bleeding, dehydration or surgery possible; no routine labs in a very well child if local pathway allows.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent abdominal ultrasound. Proceed to air/contrast enema for diagnosis and reduction when no perforation/peritonitis and expertise is available; abdominal radiograph for obstruction/perforation concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment

sections.label: Consults

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; procedural sedation support as required.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC serially, type and screen/cross, coagulation/fibrinogen, electrolytes/urea/creatinine, liver profile; stool/infectious studies and pregnancy testing when relevant.

sections.label: Imaging

sections.label: Medications / treatment

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to GI/CTU for pain requiring IV therapy, vomiting/dehydration, inability to tolerate enteral intake, organ dysfunction, or uncertain diagnosis; PICU for shock, respiratory failure, severe electrolyte disturbance, or multiorgan dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q1-2h when severe or after opioid escalation.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, pain/nausea scores, daily weight, respiratory status, abdominal examination; continuous pulse oximetry with significant opioids or respiratory compromise.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; assess for pleural effusion/ARDS in severe disease.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; consider second line if severe, frequent labs, or substantial fluid/analgesia needs.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Early isotonic IV resuscitation when depleted with frequent reassessment; begin early enteral nutrition as tolerated rather than prolonged bowel rest; avoid fluid overload.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Lipase, CBC, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, glucose, calcium, triglycerides; repeat only to monitor organ dysfunction rather than chase lipase. Cause-directed tests.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Ultrasound for biliary disease; CT/MRI only for diagnostic uncertainty, complications, or failure to improve, usually after specialist review.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Multimodal analgesia and a stepwise antiemetic plan. Ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/IV (max 8 mg) is a common first option. If nausea persists, reassess hydration, ileus, electrolyte abnormalities and complications before adding another agent; dimenhydrinate may be considered when sedation is acceptable. Avoid dopamine antagonists after prior dystonia and review QT/electrolyte risk before combination therapy. No routine antibiotics unless infected necrosis, cholangitis or another bacterial source; treat the cause. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: GI; surgery for gallstone/structural disease; PICU for severe disease; pain team if difficult control.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Pain and sedation monitoring, strict fluid balance, early feeding tolerance, glucose checks when abnormal, and respiratory observation with opioids.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess pain, perfusion, urine output, and respiratory status within 1-2h after treatment; escalate for shock, oliguria, hypoxemia, increasing abdominal distension, GI bleed, or worsening organ dysfunction.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; assess for pleural effusion/ARDS in severe disease.

sections.text: Admit to GI/CTU for moderate-severe flare, frequent bloody stools, significant anemia, dehydration, weight loss/malnutrition, severe pain, inability to tolerate oral therapy, or toxic megacolon concern; PICU for shock, perforation, severe hemorrhage, or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Monitoring

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for moderate-severe flare, IV medications, dehydration, or significant anemia.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Isotonic rehydration; enteral nutrition as tolerated with dietitian/GI guidance; NPO only for obstruction, severe ileus, perforation concern, or procedure.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, CRP/ESR, electrolytes/renal/liver profile, albumin, iron studies as appropriate; stool culture/C. difficile and other infectious testing before escalating immunosuppression.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Abdominal radiograph for severe colitis/distension or toxic megacolon concern; ultrasound/MR/CT for complications according to GI/surgery.

sections.label: Medications / treatment

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: GI early; surgery for toxic megacolon, perforation, obstruction, abscess, or refractory severe colitis; dietitian; hematology for VTE/major anemia.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess at least q4h and review daily severity score if used; escalate for tachycardia, fever, worsening distension/tenderness, reduced bowel sounds, peritonitis, falling hemoglobin, or systemic toxicity.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: As needed.

title: Feeding intolerance / vomiting in a medically complex child
summary: Admit to CTU/complex care for dehydration, recurrent emesis with aspiration risk, feed intolerance preventing medication/nutrition delivery, device complication, respiratory compromise, or caregiver concern for deviation from baseline; PICU for airway/ventilatory failure, shock, or severe neurologic change.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/complex care for dehydration, recurrent emesis with aspiration risk, feed intolerance preventing medication/nutrition delivery, device complication, respiratory compromise, or caregiver concern for deviation from baseline; PICU for airway/ventilatory failure, shock, or severe neurologic change.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if near baseline; q1-2h during respiratory, neurologic, or perfusion concern.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Compare with documented baseline; strict I&O, emesis/stool, abdominal exam, respiratory secretion burden, device function, and seizure/mental-status trend.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Continue verified home support and airway-clearance plan; involve RT early for oxygen/NIV/tracheostomy/cough-assist needs; use only equipment settings confirmed with family/chart.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain if dehydrated, unable to give essential medications, significant labs are required, or deterioration is possible.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Hold or reduce feeds initially when aspiration/obstruction is possible; provide isotonic IV hydration; restart home formula/route gradually after the cause and safety plan are clear.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Targeted glucose, electrolytes, renal function, gas, CBC/cultures, drug levels, or urinalysis based on presentation; avoid broad testing without a clinical question.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Confirm tube position or obtain abdominal/chest imaging only when device displacement, obstruction, aspiration, constipation, or another complication is suspected.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: First identify and treat device displacement, obstruction, constipation, infection, aspiration, dysmotility, pain or medication toxicity. Reconcile all home medications and time-critical drugs. Do not automatically suppress vomiting before excluding bilious obstruction, aspiration risk or tube malfunction. When an antiemetic is appropriate, ondansetron is a common first option; dimenhydrinate may be considered when sedation is acceptable. Prokinetics such as metoclopramide or domperidone require a defined dysmotility indication and local GI/pharmacy guidance. Avoid unverified substitutions and review QT/EPS risk.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Complex care/primary subspecialty, dietitian, GI/surgery/IR for tube issues, SLP for aspiration concern, palliative care when already involved; PICU early if baseline support is exceeded.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT: Document baseline versus current status, home-device settings/sizes, emergency trach/G-tube supplies, feed/med schedule, caregiver expertise, and individualized escalation plan.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after hydration, suction/airway clearance, and any feed trial; escalate for support above baseline, recurrent aspiration, bilious emesis, device dislodgement with tract concern, prolonged seizure, or caregiver report that the child is significantly unlike baseline.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Continue verified home support and airway-clearance plan; involve RT early for oxygen/NIV/tracheostomy/cough-assist needs; use only equipment settings confirmed with family/chart.

Medications/treatments: First identify and treat device displacement, obstruction, constipation, infection, aspiration, dysmotility, pain or medication toxicity. When an antiemetic is appropriate, ondansetron is a common first option; dimenhydrinate may be considered when sedation is acceptable. Prokinetics such as metoclopramide or domperidone require a defined dysmotility indication and local GI/pharmacy guidance. Avoid unverified substitutions and review QT/EPS risk.

title: Acute kidney injury (AKI)
summary: Admit to Ward if stable with close monitoring; PICU/nephrology urgently for hyperkalemia, severe acidosis, pulmonary edema, uremic symptoms, shock or dialysis consideration.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward if stable with close monitoring; PICU/nephrology urgently for hyperkalemia, severe acidosis, pulmonary edema, uremic symptoms, shock or dialysis consideration.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict hourly/shift urine output, daily weight, BP and cumulative fluid balance; cardiac monitoring for potassium abnormality.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen/ventilation for pulmonary edema; avoid fluid overload.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV access; urinary catheter only if necessary for accurate output/retention assessment.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: If hypovolemic, cautious isotonic challenge with reassessment; if euvolemic/overloaded, stop routine fluids and individualize.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Serial electrolytes/urea/creatinine/glucose/bicarbonate, calcium/phosphate/magnesium; urinalysis/microscopy, urine protein/creatinine; CK for rhabdo; hemolysis/complement/autoimmune tests as indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Renal/bladder ultrasound for obstruction or unclear AKI; source-directed imaging.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Stop nephrotoxins and renally adjust all medications; treat hyperkalemia/acidosis/pulmonary edema per emergency pathway; avoid NSAIDs. Diuretics do not cure AKI but may help overload under expert plan.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology early for stage 2â€“3, unclear intrinsic disease, significant electrolyte/overload or no improvement; PICU for dialysis-level indications.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Daily weight same scale, strict inputs/outputs, avoid potassium-containing fluids unless reviewed, pharmacy renal dosing.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess after any fluid intervention; labs q2â€“12 h depending on severity; immediate response to ECG/urine changes.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen/ventilation for pulmonary edema; avoid fluid overload.

Medications/treatments: Stop nephrotoxins and renally adjust all medications; treat hyperkalemia/acidosis/pulmonary edema per emergency pathway; avoid NSAIDs. Diuretics do not cure AKI but may help overload under expert plan.

sections.text: Admit to nephrology/CTU for hypertension, AKI, oliguria, edema, gross hematuria with systemic features, electrolyte abnormality, or uncertain diagnosis; PICU for hypertensive emergency, pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, or rapidly progressive renal failure.

sections.text: Admit to nephrology/CTU; PICU for neurologic symptoms, severe hypertension, pulmonary edema, significant bleeding, hyperkalemia, anuria, shock, or dialysis-level indications.

sections.text: Vitals: Continuous during tachycardia; q15 min after conversion until stable, then q2-4h.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/telemetry and pulse oximetry; obtain rhythm strip/12-lead ECG before and after conversion whenever this does not delay treatment.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen if hypoxemic or poorly perfused; prepare for sedation/airway support if cardioversion is required.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain IV/IO promptly; use the most proximal line possible for adenosine with immediate saline flush.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO during active unstable rhythm; cautious isotonic fluid only if preload depletion is likely because cardiomyopathy may coexist.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose, electrolytes including potassium/magnesium/calcium, CBC and thyroid tests if indicated; troponin/BNP and gas/lactate when prolonged or unstable.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph/echocardiogram when heart failure, structural disease, prolonged tachycardia or abnormal exam is present.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Stable narrow-complex regular SVT: vagal manoeuvres, then adenosine 0.1 mg/kg rapid IV push (max 6 mg) followed by flush; if unsuccessful, 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg). Unstable SVT: synchronized cardioversion 0.5-1 J/kg, then 2 J/kg if needed. Further antiarrhythmic therapy is cardiology/PICU-directed.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology for first/recurrent SVT and maintenance plan; PICU immediately for instability, refractory rhythm or ventricular dysfunction; anesthesia if cardioversion sedation is needed.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Save rhythm strips, apply defibrillation pads early if unstable, record exact rates/medication times, teach family pulse/recurrence plan when appropriate.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Confirm sustained sinus rhythm and perfusion after each intervention. Recurrent SVT, hypotension, altered mental status, chest pain, pulmonary edema or poor perfusion requires immediate synchronized cardioversion/PICU.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen if hypoxemic or poorly perfused; prepare for sedation/airway support if cardioversion is required.

Medications/treatments: Stable narrow-complex regular SVT: vagal manoeuvres, then adenosine 0.1 mg/kg rapid IV push (max 6 mg) followed by flush; if unsuccessful, 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg). Unstable SVT: synchronized cardioversion 0.5-1 J/kg, then 2 J/kg if needed. Further antiarrhythmic therapy is cardiology/PICU-directed.

title: Syncope
summary: Admit to monitored ward for exertional/supine syncope, abnormal ECG, known heart disease, family history of sudden death, significant injury, persistent symptoms, recurrent unexplained events or concerning neurologic/metabolic findings; PICU for instability or malignant arrhythmia.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored ward for exertional/supine syncope, abnormal ECG, known heart disease, family history of sudden death, significant injury, persistent symptoms, recurrent unexplained events or concerning neurologic/metabolic findings; PICU for instability or malignant arrhythmia.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; obtain orthostatic HR/BP when safe and clinically relevant.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Telemetry for cardiac red flags/abnormal ECG; fall precautions; neuro checks if head injury or incomplete recovery.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; oxygen for hypoxemia or cardiopulmonary cause.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Not routine for classic vasovagal syncope; obtain for dehydration, abnormal labs, recurrent event or concerning cause.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Oral hydration and salt when vasovagal/orthostatic pattern; isotonic IV fluid for clinically significant dehydration; regular diet unless procedure planned.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Bedside glucose and pregnancy test when applicable; CBC/electrolytes/toxicology only when suggested by history/exam. Do not order indiscriminate panels.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine neuroimaging. Echocardiography for abnormal exam/ECG, exertional syncope or cardiac history; head imaging only for significant trauma or neurologic concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat identified cause; stop/review QT-prolonging or hypotensive medications; no empiric antiseizure or cardiac medication for uncomplicated vasovagal syncope.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology for exertional/supine episodes, abnormal ECG, palpitations, family history or structural disease; neurology only when seizure/neurologic disorder remains likely.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Document prodrome, position, duration, colour, movements and recovery; supervised ambulation until stable; hydration tracking.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review ECG personally and reassess before discharge planning. Recurrent event on monitor, ventricular arrhythmia, long QT/Brugada/WPW pattern, chest pain, dyspnea or persistent neurologic deficit requires urgent escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; oxygen for hypoxemia or cardiopulmonary cause.
Medications/treatments: Treat identified cause; stop/review QT-prolonging or hypotensive medications; no empiric antiseizure or cardiac medication for uncomplicated vasovagal syncope.

title: Myocarditis / pericarditis
summary: Admit to cardiology/monitored unit; PICU for ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmia, hypotension, rising lactate, respiratory distress, altered mental status, or significant pericardial effusion/tamponade concern.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to cardiology/monitored unit; PICU for ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmia, hypotension, rising lactate, respiratory distress, altered mental status, or significant pericardial effusion/tamponade concern.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially, then q2-4h only after stability is clear.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous telemetry and pulse oximetry; strict I&O, perfusion, chest pain, hepatomegaly, and rhythm trend.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen as needed; use positive pressure cautiously in severe cardiac dysfunction and involve PICU.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; consider second line if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Avoid routine fluid boluses unless clear hypovolemia; use cautious isotonic fluids with repeated cardiac assessment. Sodium/fluid restriction if heart failure.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Troponin, BNP/NT-proBNP, CBC, electrolytes including magnesium, renal/liver profile, CRP/ESR, gas/lactate if ill; infectious/autoimmune tests with cardiology.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: ECG and echocardiogram; chest radiograph; cardiac MRI when stable and recommended by cardiology.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Activity restriction; treat heart failure/arrhythmia per cardiology; anti-inflammatory therapy for uncomplicated pericarditis when appropriate; avoid unnecessary catecholamine-provoking medications. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology urgently; PICU early for dysfunction/arrhythmia; rheumatology/ID when etiology requires.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Telemetry review, strict fluid balance, chest pain/rhythm documentation, minimal exertion, and immediate reporting of syncope or perfusion change.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess frequently with repeat ECG/biomarkers/echo as directed; escalate for ventricular arrhythmia, heart block, hypotension, rising lactate, worsening hepatomegaly, pulmonary edema, muffled heart sounds, or pulsus/tamponade features.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen as needed; use positive pressure cautiously in severe cardiac dysfunction and involve PICU.

Medications/treatments: Activity restriction; treat heart failure/arrhythmia per cardiology; anti-inflammatory therapy for uncomplicated pericarditis when appropriate; avoid unnecessary catecholamine-provoking medications. Verify doses.

title: Heart failure / congenital heart disease decompensation
summary: Admit to cardiology/monitored unit; PICU for significant oxygen/support above baseline, shock, severe work of breathing, altered mental status, arrhythmia, duct-dependent physiology concern, or escalating diuretics/inotropes.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to cardiology/monitored unit; PICU for significant oxygen/support above baseline, shock, severe work of breathing, altered mental status, arrhythmia, duct-dependent physiology concern, or escalating diuretics/inotropes.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h until trajectory is clear; include pre/post-ductal saturations in infants when relevant and compare with baseline targets.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, strict I&O, daily weight, perfusion, hepatomegaly, feeding tolerance, and respiratory effort.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Use the child-specific oxygen saturation target; excessive oxygen may be harmful in selected mixing lesions. Continue verified home oxygen/NIV and involve RT/cardiology.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; second access if unstable. Avoid excessive agitation in fragile physiology.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Follow cardiac fluid/sodium plan; consider NPO with IV fluids if severe distress, but avoid both dehydration and fluid overload. Feeding support for infants with increased work.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, electrolytes/renal/liver profile, glucose, blood gas/lactate if ill, BNP/NT-proBNP as useful; drug levels when indicated; cultures if infection may have triggered decompensation.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: ECG, chest radiograph, echocardiogram per cardiology; device interrogation when relevant.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Continue verified essential cardiac medications unless contraindicated; diuretics/afterload/inotrope therapy per cardiology; treat trigger such as infection or anemia. Verify all doses and home formulation.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology immediately; PICU for any instability; cardiac surgery/device team when relevant; dietitian/feeding team for chronic growth issues.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT: Document baseline saturation/support, medication times, weights, urine output, feeds, hepatomegaly, edema, and parent-reported early signs of decompensation.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after each intervention and at least q2h initially; escalate for worsening cyanosis, weak pulses, rising lactate, oliguria, new gallop, arrhythmia, increasing hepatomegaly, apnea, or support above unit capability.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Use the child-specific oxygen saturation target; excessive oxygen may be harmful in selected mixing lesions. Continue verified home oxygen/NIV and involve RT/cardiology.

Medications/treatments: Continue verified essential cardiac medications unless contraindicated; diuretics/afterload/inotrope therapy per cardiology; treat trigger such as infection or anemia. Verify all doses and home formulation.

title: Rhabdomyolysis
summary: Admit for significant CK elevation with symptoms, pigmenturia, AKI/electrolyte abnormality, inability to hydrate orally, ongoing muscle injury or high-risk cause; PICU for severe hyperkalemia, arrhythmia, shock or compartment syndrome.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit for significant CK elevation with symptoms, pigmenturia, AKI/electrolyte abnormality, inability to hydrate orally, ongoing muscle injury or high-risk cause; PICU for severe hyperkalemia, arrhythmia, shock or compartment syndrome.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q1-2h during severe electrolyte abnormality or aggressive fluid therapy.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict intake/output with urine output target, daily weight, serial limb/neurovascular exams and cardiac monitoring when potassium is abnormal.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; support systemic cause/toxidrome as needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for isotonic fluids and serial labs.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Start isotonic IV crystalloid, commonly 1.5-2 times maintenance and titrate to urine output/clinical status; avoid potassium-containing fluids initially. Routine bicarbonate/mannitol is not recommended without a specific indication.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CK, electrolytes including potassium/calcium/phosphate, urea/creatinine, bicarbonate, urinalysis, AST/ALT; ECG for hyperkalemia. Repeat CK/electrolytes/renal function q6-12h initially based on severity.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Not routine; ultrasound/MRI/compartment-pressure evaluation for focal trauma, infection or compartment syndrome.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Stop offending drug/exertion, treat hyperthermia/seizure/infection, manage hyperkalemia immediately using emergency protocol, avoid nephrotoxins/NSAIDs.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology for AKI, refractory electrolyte abnormality or dialysis concern; surgery/orthopedics for compartment syndrome; toxicology/metabolic genetics for relevant cause.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Accurate urine output/colour, fluid-balance and limb pain/swelling checks; avoid potassium supplements and nephrotoxins.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Trend CK, potassium, creatinine and urine output. Oliguria, rising potassium/creatinine, ECG change, severe hypocalcemic symptoms or tense painful compartment requires urgent escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; support systemic cause/toxidrome as needed.
Medications/treatments: Stop offending drug/exertion, treat hyperthermia/seizure/infection, manage hyperkalemia immediately using emergency protocol, avoid nephrotoxins/NSAIDs.

title: Anaphylaxis
summary: Admit/observe in a monitored setting after stabilization; PICU for shock, airway edema, repeated epinephrine, ongoing bronchospasm, arrhythmia, or need for epinephrine infusion.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit/observe in a monitored setting after stabilization; PICU for shock, airway edema, repeated epinephrine, ongoing bronchospasm, arrhythmia, or need for epinephrine infusion.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous monitoring during active symptoms; repeat BP, perfusion, respiratory and skin assessment every 5-15 min until clearly stable, then space according to risk.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry and cardiac monitoring; strict documentation of epinephrine times, BP and symptom response.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen, airway positioning and early difficult-airway planning for voice change, stridor, tongue/oropharyngeal swelling, or progressive obstruction; inhaled salbutamol for persistent bronchospasm after epinephrine.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain promptly for moderate-severe reaction; two IVs/IO if shock.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO during airway risk. For persistent hypotension give isotonic crystalloid 20 mL/kg rapidly and reassess; repeat judiciously while preparing vasoactive support.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Diagnosis is clinical; no routine labs. Consider tryptase according to allergy pathway without delaying treatment; obtain gas/lactate/electrolytes if shock.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: IM epinephrine 1 mg/mL (1:1000) at 0.01 mg/kg = 0.01 mL/kg into anterolateral thigh (max 0.5 mg), repeat every 5-15 min as needed. Antihistamines and corticosteroids are adjuncts only and must never delay epinephrine. Start titrated IV epinephrine infusion in refractory shock with PICU.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior/RT immediately; PICU/anesthesia for airway or circulatory compromise; allergy referral before discharge planning.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Keep epinephrine and airway cart at bedside; lay flat with legs elevated unless respiratory distress/vomiting; do not allow sudden standing; record likely trigger and biphasic-risk features.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess 5 min after each epinephrine dose. Observe at least 4-6 h after symptom resolution, longer/overnight for severe reaction, delayed epinephrine, multiple doses, asthma, remote access, or biphasic-risk factors.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen, airway positioning and early difficult-airway planning for voice change, stridor, tongue/oropharyngeal swelling, or progressive obstruction; inhaled salbutamol for persistent bronchospasm after epinephrine.

Medications/treatments: IM epinephrine 1 mg/mL (1:1000) at 0.01 mg/kg = 0.01 mL/kg into anterolateral thigh (max 0.5 mg), repeat every 5-15 min as needed. Antihistamines and corticosteroids are adjuncts only and must never delay epinephrine. Start titrated IV epinephrine infusion in refractory shock with PICU.

title: Allergic reaction without anaphylaxis
summary: Admit to Ward observation if stable; upgrade immediately if any respiratory/circulatory involvement or multisystem progression.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward observation if stable; upgrade immediately if any respiratory/circulatory involvement or multisystem progression.

sections.label: Respiratory support

sections.label: Labs

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess within 30â€“60 minutes and before discharge.
